title: Projeto Através dos Espectros (2026-2027). Parte 1 - O início
authors: Lauro Cézar Montefalco de Lira Santos
Emannuel Felinto Ranon Julio Cesar Marinho
abstract: O projeto de extensão Através dos Espectros, iniciado em 2025, na Universidade Federal de Pernambuco, continua suas atividades em 2026 e 2027, a fim de popularizar, cada vez mais, o Sensoriamento Remoto Geológico. A presente obra apresenta, de forma amigável e divertida, os objetivos do segundo ano de atuação do projeto, a equipe executora e os principais produtos focados.

title: Analisis Sentimen Komentar YouTube tentang Pengolahan Sampah Plastik Menggunakan Support Vector Machine dan Random Forest
abstract: Perkembangan media sosial menyediakan ruang bagi pengguna untuk menyampaikan tanggapan terhadap berbagai isu, termasuk pengolahan sampah plastik menjadi bahan bakar. Komentar pada YouTube dapat dimanfaatkan sebagai sumber data untuk menganalisis kecenderungan sentimen pengguna terhadap suatu topik. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis sentimen komentar YouTube tentang pengolahan sampah plastik serta membandingkan kinerja algoritma Support Vector Machine (SVM) dan Random Forest. Data penelitian diperoleh melalui proses scraping komentar pada video berjudul “Sulap Sampah Plastik Jadi Bensin RON 92 & Solar. Solusi Cerdas Atasi Limbah” pada kanal Tanilink TV. Sebanyak 1.413 komentar dianalisis melalui tahapan pre-processing, pelabelan sentimen menggunakan pendekatan berbasis leksikon (lexicon-based), ekstraksi fitur teks, pembagian data latih dan data uji dengan rasio 70:30, serta klasifikasi menggunakan SVM dan Random Forest. Hasil pelabelan menunjukkan bahwa 939 komentar (66,45%) dikategorikan sebagai sentimen negatif dan 474 komentar (33,55%) sebagai sentimen positif. Hasil evaluasi menunjukkan bahwa SVM memperoleh akurasi sebesar 85,1% dan weighted F1-score sebesar 0,848, sedangkan Random Forest memperoleh akurasi sebesar 82,5% dan weighted F1-score sebesar 0,818. Berdasarkan hasil pengujian pada dataset yang digunakan, SVM menunjukkan kinerja lebih baik daripada Random Forest. Temuan ini terbatas pada komentar dari video yang dianalisis dan belum dapat digeneralisasikan untuk menggambarkan opini masyarakat secara keseluruhan.

title: Perbandingan RoBERTa dan Lexicon-Based untuk Pseudo-Labeling Sentimen Komentar YouTube dengan Machine Learning
abstract: Penelitian ini bertujuan membandingkan pendekatan RoBERTa dan Lexicon-Based dalam menghasilkan pseudo-label sentimen komentar YouTube serta mengevaluasi kinerja algoritma machine learning dalam mengklasifikasikan label yang dihasilkan. Data penelitian berasal dari komentar pada video “Presiden Prabowo Menjawab (PART 2): Efisiensi, Pertaruhan MBG & Reformasi Kepolisian” dari Mata Najwa. Setelah proses penyaringan dan preprocessing, diperoleh 2.850 komentar yang dianalisis. Penelitian menerapkan dua jalur preprocessing, yaitu pemrosesan minimal pada RoBERTa untuk mempertahankan konteks kalimat serta pemrosesan tambahan pada Lexicon-Based melalui tokenisasi dan penghapusan stopword. Label sentimen yang dihasilkan oleh kedua pendekatan digunakan untuk melatih dan mengevaluasi algoritma Support Vector Machine (SVM), Naïve Bayes, dan Neural Network menggunakan fitur Term Frequency–Inverse Document Frequency (TF-IDF). Hasil evaluasi menunjukkan bahwa pada dataset berlabel RoBERTa, Neural Network memperoleh nilai accuracy sebesar 0,7333 dan F1-score sebesar 0,6024. Sementara itu, pada dataset berlabel Lexicon-Based, SVM menghasilkan accuracy sebesar 0,6439 dan F1-score sebesar 0,6323. Dengan demikian, Neural Network menghasilkan accuracy tertinggi pada dataset berlabel RoBERTa, sedangkan SVM menghasilkan F1-score tertinggi pada dataset berlabel Lexicon-Based. Perbedaan hasil tersebut menunjukkan adanya variasi kinerja klasifikasi pada kedua skema pelabelan otomatis. Namun, karena evaluasi didasarkan pada label hasil pseudo-labeling, nilai metrik tersebut menggambarkan kemampuan model dalam mereplikasi label otomatis dan belum secara langsung membuktikan ketepatan klasifikasi terhadap sentimen sebenarnya. Validasi menggunakan anotasi manusia diperlukan untuk menilai kualitas label dan memperkuat kesimpulan penelitian.

title: AutoCare AI: An AI-Assisted Vehicle Service Management System
abstract: Independent garages commonly manage repairs with paper job cards, verbal estimates and memory, so the accuracy and efficiency of their service cannot be measured. This paper presents AutoCare AI, a zero-cost web application built with Flutter and Firebase that digitises the garage workflow from walk-in to invoice, estimates a job's fault category, labour time and cost from the customer's free-text complaint using Google Gemini (with a keyword-rule engine for offline demonstration), suggests the least-busy suitable mechanic, predicts each vehicle's next periodic service and records manual, AI and actual outcomes on every job. The study follows a design-science approach with secondary, quantitative data: 31,236 owner complaints from the public NHTSA complaints database, labelled into seven of the application's fault categories and split into 24,988 training and 6,248 test records. A TF-IDF and Logistic Regression classifier reached 90.6 % accuracy (macro-F1 0.907), significantly above an 80 % target (exact binomial p ≈ 1.09 × 10⁻¹¹⁵), whereas the application's keyword rules reached only 57.6 %. The learned classifier was significantly more accurate than the rules (exact McNemar, 2,199 against 136 discordant pairs, p < 0.001). In a 250-day simulation, greedy assignment lowered the mean daily spread of mechanic workload to 1.49 h against 4.03 h for random assignment (Wilcoxon p ≈ 3.85 × 10⁻⁴²). Gemini was not evaluated at scale because AI was kept switched off to guarantee zero cost; its few live estimates are reported only as anecdotal evidence.

title: Beyond the Benchmark: Conditioning, Domains and Failure Modes of Qwen3-TTS
abstract: Qwen3-TTS reports state-of-the-art zero-shot voice cloning, but its technical report leaves open how the model should be conditioned, how it behaves outside read speech, and how it fails. We characterise its two cloning interfaces, in-context learning (ICL) and X-Vector, against Chatterbox, XTTS-v2 and F5-TTS on read, meeting, emotional and air-traffic-control (ATC) speech, using eighteen objective measures, an LLM judge, a spoofing countermeasure and a listening test. Neither interface dominates: ICL clones timbre more closely from correctly transcribed references, X-Vector clones timing, and ICL degrades sharply when a short reference transcript is wrong. Domain explains four times more variance than system choice. Qwen3-TTS leads on intelligibility and pitch register but trails on prosody, and the objective measures rank systems differently from listeners. An off-the-shelf countermeasure flags its clones no more often than genuine recordings, and on ATC radio it fails for every system. Code and audio are released.

title: Towards Looped Models Done Right, Part I: Topology, Input Injection, Recurrent-State Design
abstract: Looped language models reuse physical Transformer blocks across logical depth, but established architectures entangle recurrence placement, input injection, and recurrent state organization. We isolate these axes in models trained from scratch at matched parameter scale, logical depth, and token budgets, and then test whether the resulting design principles transfer to resident- and active-parameter-matched Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models. The prelude-recurrent block-coda sandwich architecture consistently improves performance on context extraction and reasoning-intensive tasks. Input injection primarily enhances knowledge retrieval and context utilization, whereas random initialization and separate H/L recurrent states provide mixed or negative returns. Taken together, these results favor the Huginn-style design: at the 730M-parameter and 336B-token scale, the complete Huginn architecture outperforms Ouro across all ten benchmarks. The advantages of Huginn over Ouro transfer to MoE models. At the 8BA0.8B (32BA3B when unrolled) scale trained on 500B tokens, Huginn outperforms Ouro on nearly all benchmarks spanning knowledge, reasoning, and coding, while also exhibiting more balanced expert routing. Under matched training and inference FLOPs, the Huginn-style model uses 75% fewer resident parameters than a 112-layer feedforward MoE baseline. Despite its smaller physical parameters, it outperforms the feedforward baseline on DROP and GSM8K, matches it on MATH500, and remains competitive on the other benchmarks.

title: Understanding, Improving, and Applying Self-Supervised Neural Representations
abstract: Human beings are known to develop a rich understanding of the visual world by simply being exposed to it and without constant explicit supervision. Although the mechanisms underlying this ability are not fully understood, Self-Supervised Learning (SSL) is an attempt to endow machines with a similar ability, by learning from unlabeled data using supervisory signals latent within the data. SSL has become a powerful paradigm for visual representation learning, but important questions remain about whether the learned representations are sufficiently expressive for downstream tasks, how such representations can be improved after pre-training, and how the composition of the pre-training data itself affects their usefulness. This thesis studies these questions from three complementary perspectives: scientific applications, representation desiderata and methods for improvement, and data-curation principles for real-world scenarios. First, we apply SSL to the task of automatic terrain categorization in Martian terrain images. Using deep self-supervised clustering, we show how neural networks can learn meaningful geomorphological and textural features from a large pool of unlabeled images, enabling the creation of a large dataset of Martian terrain images with scientifically relevant and granular terrain categories without the need for exhaustive expert annotation. We further validate the scientific significance of the discovered categories with expert input and create a detailed terrain taxonomy to encourage more fundamental analyses in the future. Second, we propose a general-purpose information-theoretic criterion for improving the quality of already-trained, highly optimized SSL representations. By maximizing the entropy of SSL-trained embeddings in a compact space, we prepare them as well as possible for future, as-yet-unknown, discrimination tasks. Our criterion is defined in terms of easy-to-estimate, low-dimensional constraints. We show that even without explicitly enforcing higher-dimensional constraints in our criterion, this approach yields practically useful embeddings and improves downstream performance without introducing extensive training overhead. Finally, we study how the composition of pre-training data shapes the usefulness of SSL representations for a given downstream task under finite compute and model-capacity constraints. Specifically, we examine how the diversity and relevance of the pre-training images, and their relative concentrations affect downstream performance while isolating common confounding factors. We propose a systematic framework with three data-composition axes—purity, distraction, and abundance—and use it to conduct carefully controlled experiments on a focused set of SSL models, datasets, and tasks. Our results refine the prevailing notion that larger pre-training datasets are necessarily better, and suggest that data curation should be treated as a first-order design variable in compute- or capacity-constrained regimes.

title: A Controlled Decomposition of Training-Data Quantity and Class Allocation: Minority-Class Reliability in Medical Image Classification
abstract: In medical image classification, an accurate model is not the same as a trustworthy one, and in imbalanced settings the rare class is usually the one that matters. Aggregate and rank-based summaries average over a test set dominated by the majority class, so they can look acceptable while reliability on the minority class has broken. The usual study of imbalance also conflates two things: how much training data there is, and how it is allocated across classes. We separate them with a controlled decomposition on the training-data plane spanned by the minority and majority counts. Four protocols vary total quantity at balance, allocation at a fixed budget, majority exposure at a fixed minority, and minority availability at a fixed majority. Three models, from a linear baseline to a residual network, are trained from scratch under a fixed compute budget, with multiple seeds per condition as a variability estimate. Reliability is measured class-conditionally alongside the pooled summaries, and two post-hoc remedies, temperature scaling and known-prior correction, are tested against the minority gap. PatchCamelyon is the primary dataset, with ISIC 2020 as a secondary check under natural imbalance. As allocation moved from balance, pooled summaries could stay acceptable while minority recall collapsed and minority calibration deteriorated; the class split exposed the failure. Temperature scaling did not remove the class-conditional gap; known-prior correction largely closed its threshold part for the two convolutional models and over-corrected the linear one. Keywords: model calibration, class imbalance, class-conditional reliability, medical image classification, histopathology, selective prediction

title: 比尔密码第1页破解出的部分明文
abstract: 根据《比尔密码的破解方法》,我们使用DeepSeek尝试破解比尔密码第1页,得到部分明文,可解析出部分片段,但是我们不熟悉英文,无法破解出整篇内容。虽然如此,但是由此可见,按照我们的方法,证明比尔密码是可以破解的,下一步,需要熟悉英文的人们努力破解了。

title: Do Neuromodulator-Inspired State Prompts Generalize Across LLM Families? A Publicly Preregistered Audit of Output Length, Semantic Breadth, and Instruction Equivalence
abstract: Completed results, manuscript and full reproduction package for the publicly preregistered Route B study (preregistration: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22655376, published before any formal target output was generated). Using official GLM-5.2 and Qwen3.8-Max-0902 APIs, the study crossed 24 Chinese open-ended tasks, eight component-matched prompt conditions, four repetitions and two target models (1,536 fresh-session responses). The rich fatigue package shortened responses relative to neutral in both models (GLM -0.314, 95% CI [-0.383, -0.247]; Qwen -0.349 [-0.394, -0.302]; one-sided exact p = 5.96e-8 in each), and the rich curiosity package increased condition-blind semantic breadth in both (GLM +1.083 [0.562, 1.583]; Qwen +0.708 [0.458, 0.953]). Rich-direct practical equivalence did not pass the cross-model rule for either construct: fatigue equivalence held only in GLM and curiosity equivalence only in Qwen, so both fixed sequences stopped. Machine ratings were highly repeatable but agreed only moderately with a blind author validation sample. A procedural ordering deviation during sealing of the blind review is disclosed in the manuscript and package. The manuscript PDF (v0.3, dated 23 September 2026) predates this deposit; its data-availability statement that results were not yet public is superseded by this record. The package is split into four archives because of upload limits; extract all four into one folder. Results concern observable outputs only and do not establish emotion, consciousness, biological neuromodulation, persistent state or identical internal computation.

title: A Secure Proxy Re-encryption Framework for Confidential and Cache-friendly Content Delivery Networks
abstract: secure segmented-video delivery requires confidentiality while retaining cache usability.CDN-PRE integrates 2-of-3 threshold proxy re-encryption, encrypted caching, recipient-specific delegation, and client-side decryption in a Docker-based prototype.Sequential evaluations comprised 3,800,000 requests, with scaled-resource mean latency of 55.57-59.97ms.Separate sequential stress tests extended workloads to 400 logical clients.Fixedresource true-concurrency tests covered 50-200 clients under Cold, Warm10, and Full-Warm conditions.CDN-PRE demonstrated the most stable throughput across increasing workloads, with throughput variability of 1.411%, retaining 97.18% of its C50 throughput at C200 despite increasing tail latency pressure.Under Zipf workloads, increasing bounded LRU cache capacity raised hit ratios by 19.49-26.91 percentage points and reduced mean latency by 11.2-14.6%,with ≈ 100% success across 2,000,000 requests.Adversarial tests recorded no unauthorized plaintext recovery within the evaluated threat model.Packet captures measured a selected TCP-payload control-traffic share of approximately 1.67%.These results support confidential, cache-compatible delivery while identifying saturation and resource trade-offs.

title: Rigorous Engineering of Collective Adaptive Systems (in the Age of Pervasive AI): Introduction to the 6th Track Edition
abstract: Abstract Collective Adaptive Systems (CAS) are characterised by the interaction of autonomous entities that collectively adapt to dynamic and open-ended environments. Their development poses significant engineering challenges, requiring sound methodologies, formal models, and effective tool support. This introduction reviews the scope of the 6 th edition of the track “Rigorous Engineering of Collective Adaptive Systems”, outlines the panel discussion, and provides an overview of the 25 scientific contributions grouped by nine thematic sessions: Autonomy, Knowledge, and Emergence; Decision-Making and Awareness; Generative AI and Reasoning; Rigorous CAS Engineering in the Quantum-AI Era; Quantitative Modelling and Simulation; Modular Design and Platform Architectures; Engineering Robotic Systems; Programming and Coordinating Robotic Systems; and Modelling Cyber-Physical Systems. Taken together, the contributions illustrate a growing convergence between formal modelling, data-driven techniques, compositional architectures, runtime assurance, and human-centred governance.

title: Agentic Physics-Grounded Video Generation via Memory-Augmented In-Context Reasoning
abstract: Physical plausibility is essential for realistic video generation. Existing methods impose physical guidance before synthesis via simulations or refined prompts, but this can limit dynamic diversity, miss errors that emerge only after generation, and require repeated regeneration when inconsistencies remain. We therefore study a generate-diagnose-repair paradigm that preserves the original generation capability and selectively repairs physical inconsistencies afterward, raising two key questions: what to repair and how to repair? To address them, we introduce PhysRepair, an agentic video generation framework that combines causal reasoning over the observed physical failure with prior repair experience to enable localized and adaptive correction. Specifically, Spatiotemporal Causal Constraints identify the first invalid physical state and its causally affected states, producing a repair specification that guides physically plausible local regeneration while preserving unaffected content. Experience-augmented In-context Learning combines the ongoing repair context with relevant experience from previous repairs, allowing the agent to adapt its repair decisions across diverse physical failures and accumulate completed trajectories for future cases. Experiments on Physics-IQ Verified across solid mechanics, fluid dynamics, optics, thermodynamics, and magnetism demonstrate that PhysRepair consistently improves the physical plausibility of generated videos over existing methods. Our project page is available at https://xxkkxxx.github.io/PhysRepair-Website/.

title: ECHO: Replacing the Compliance Proxy with Response Harmfulness in Optimization-Based Jailbreak Attack
abstract: Despite extensive safety alignment, large language models remain vulnerable to jailbreak attacks. Existing optimization-based attacks share a single objective: maximize a token-level proxy of victim compliance---such as the likelihood of an affirmative prefix---computed on the prompt rather than the decoded reply. This proxy cannot distinguish a cautious hedge from a fully actionable harmful answer, leaving the search blind to what the model actually says. We propose ECHO (Evaluation-Conditioned Harmfulness Optimization), which replaces the compliance proxy with response-level, continuous harmfulness scores from HarmSig, a 1.7B regressor grounded in actual harmful capability. ECHO couples HarmSig with five word-level perturbation operators and Keyword-Anchored Beam Search with global top-m memory, under a strict black-box threat model. Across five open-weight victims on AdvBench, ECHO achieves up to 0.898 StrongREJECT mean score and 89.23% HarmBench success. Our code is publicly available at https://github.com/STANWYW/echo.

title: O'ZBEK TILI MILLIY KORPUSIDA LINGVISTIK GESHTALTNI AVTOMATIK ANIQLASH VA ULARNING KOGNITIV-SEMANTIK ONTOLOGIYASINI YARATISH
abstract: Annotatsiya. Ushbu maqolada O‘zbek tili milliy korpusi ma’lumotlari asosida lingvistik geshtaltlarni avtomatik aniqlash va ularning kognitiv-semantik ontologiyasini yaratish usullari ko‘rib chiqiladi. Tadqiqotda korpusdagi katta matnlar bazasidan statistik va kollokatsion ko‘rsatkichlar yordamida markaziy so‘zlar atrofidagi turg‘un birikmalar va iboralarni avtomatik ajratib olish algoritmi ishlab chiqilgan. Shuningdek, ajratilgan geshtaltlarni sun’iy intellekt va tabiiy tilni qayta ishlash tizimlari uchun bilimlarni rasmiylashtirish muhitida ontologik model ko‘rinishiga keltirish yo‘llari ko‘rsatilgan Kalit so‘zlar: lingvistik geshtalt, o‘zbek tili milliy korpusi, kognitiv-semantik ontologiya, tabiiy tilni qayta ishlash, kollokatsiya, semantik model. Аннотация. В данной статье рассматриваются методы автоматического извлечения лингвистических гештальтов и создания их когнитивно-семантической онтологии на основе данных Национального корпуса узбекского языка. В исследовании разработан алгоритм автоматического выделения устойчивых словосочетаний и фраз вокруг ключевых слов из больших текстовых массивов корпуса с использованием статистических и коллокационных показателей. Также предложены способы представления выделенных гештальтов в виде онтологической модели в среде формализации знаний для систем искусственного интеллекта и обработки естественного языка. Ключевые слова: лингвистический гештальт, Национальный корпус узбекского языка, когнитивно-семантическая онтология, обработка естественного языка, коллокация, семантическая модель. Abstract. This article examines methods for automatically extracting linguistic gestalts and building their cognitive-semantic ontology based on data from the Uzbek National Corpus. The study presents an algorithm that utilizes statistical and collocational metrics to automatically extract stable collocations and phrases surrounding core words from large corpus text datasets. Additionally, it demonstrates ways to represent the extracted gestalts as an ontological model within a knowledge formalization environment for artificial intelligence and Natural Language Processing systems. Keywords: linguistic gestalt, Uzbek National Corpus, cognitive-semantic ontology, Natural Language Processing, collocation, semantic model.

title: HACK-2 'The Poisoned Well': Sanctioned Synthetic Hackathon — Upstream Context-Poisoning and Forged-Authority Attack Classes Against a Deterministic Governance Gate (5/5 Preregistered Falsifiers, Receipt-First)
abstract: SQUIRL OS RESEARCH DISCLOSURE — READ FIRST: This work was produced inside an AI-assisted, receipt-first research program (open-book doctrine: audit-and-correction, versioned amendments, append-only public ledger). Prereg amended to v1.1 forward-only, reason disclosed (commit 64e71c7). title: Computational Complexity of Self-Attention Algorithms for Efficient Transformer Architectures
abstract: Self-attention is fundamental to Transformer architectures, but its computational and memory requirements grow quadratically with sequence length. This paper presents a structured narrative review of computationally efficient self-attention algorithms. It establishes the mathematical foundations of standard self-attention and examines dense, sparse/local, low-rank projection, landmark/Nyström, kernel/linear, memory-efficient exact, and hierarchical mechanisms. The review compares these approaches in terms of arithmetic complexity, memory requirements, sequence-length scaling, approximation, connectivity, I/O behaviour, implementation overhead, and hardware dependence. It distinguishes algorithmic complexity reduction from implementation-level optimization and clarifies the conditions under which complexity is linear in sequence length. Analytical crossover conditions show how sequence length, representation dimension, mechanism-specific parameters, and implementation overhead influence practical advantage. The review demonstrates that efficient attention cannot be characterized solely as quadratic versus linear complexity and identifies research gaps in multidimensional complexity modelling, approximation-error trade-offs, I/O complexity, long-range dependency preservation, Pareto efficiency, and hardware-aware analysis.

title: Qanela: A framework proposal for designing portable quantum assembly languages across different quantum computing platforms
abstract: The diversity of quantum hardware platforms creates significant algorithm portability challenges, with each platform employing distinct instruction sets, gate implementations, and physical constraints that hinder software reusability. This paper presents a framework for designing portable quantum assembly languages enabling seamless cross-platform execution. Through systematic profiling of Shor’s, Grover’s, and QAOA algorithms on IBM Qiskit, Microsoft Q#, and Google Cirq — 3,216 executions of identical, reference-validated logical circuits — we identify key portability challenges and derive empirically grounded design criteria from execution-pattern analysis. With matched workloads, cross-platform circuit-depth divergence is 1.3–1.6× where no gate decomposition is required and rises to 94.8× under multi-controlled decomposition pressure, of which 3.36× is genuine same-level synthesis divergence and the remainder an abstraction-level measurement gap; optimization semantics, topology expressibility, and quantum–classical execution contracts diverge analogously. The framework balances hardware abstraction with performance optimization through declared abstraction levels, topology-aware compilation, optimization profiles with defined semantics, and a universal gate set with platform-specific decomposition. Prototype validation demonstrates 100% automated compilation of unmodified single-source programs across 30 platform configurations, with all 90 executions passing calibrated distributional acceptance gates and exact statevector fidelity of 1.000000 against the language’s reference semantics, providing feasibility evidence for vendor-independent quantum software development.

With matched workloads, cross-platform circuit-depth divergence is 1.3–1.6× where no gate decomposition is required and rises to 94.8× under multi-controlled decomposition pressure, of which 3.36× is genuine same-level synthesis divergence and the remainder an abstraction-level measurement gap; optimization semantics, topology expressibility, and quantum–classical execution contracts diverge analogously. The framework balances hardware abstraction with performance optimization through declared abstraction levels, topology-aware compilation, optimization profiles with defined semantics, and a universal gate set with platform-specific decomposition. Prototype validation demonstrates 100% automated compilation of unmodified single-source programs across 30 platform configurations, with all 90 executions passing calibrated distributional acceptance gates and exact statevector fidelity of 1.000000 against the language’s reference semantics, providing feasibility evidence for vendor-independent quantum software development.

title: On the possibilities and limitations of LLM-based multi-agent systems for multi-criteria decision-making in healthcare operations management
abstract: Multi-criteria models for healthcare operations need weights that express how stakeholders trade off patient waiting time, provider workload, and operating cost, but these weights are difficult to quantify. Teams of large language model (LLM) agents, each prompted to represent a stakeholder, have been used to supply them. We propose a framework for assessing the reliability of LLM-generated preferences as inputs to multi-objective optimization and quantifying how their uncertainty affects decisions. We study explicit preferences by asking agents to rate the importance of the criteria in an outpatient appointment scheduling problem, and implicit preferences by inferring trade-offs from the agents' pairwise choices between emergency department configurations. The computational experiments show that the explicit preferences respond to the clinic's operating conditions and differ across roles, but deliberation among the agents can erase these differences, whereas simple averaging preserves them. The pairwise choices used to reveal the agents' implicit preferences depend largely on which option is presented first, and we find limited evidence that a statistical model using contextual information alongside presentation order predicts the agents' choices on new comparison pairs better than a model using presentation order alone. We then formulate robust weighted-sum optimization models to account for preference uncertainty. In most cases, these models select different schedules or configurations from those obtained using average preference weights. These results indicate that LLM-generated preferences need an audit of this kind before they are used as optimization weights in healthcare decision support.

title: VLA-Fabric: Learning Interaction for Composable Multi-Arm VLA Agents
abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models are rapidly expanding what individual robots can accomplish, yet many real-world manipulation settings require multiple arms to operate as a coordinated system. Existing approaches organize multi-arm coordination in different ways, including centralized joint policies, high-level task or role assignment, and locally executed policies that react to teammates. However, how complete action-producing VLAs should explicitly interact with one another during action generation remains largely unexplored. We introduce VLA-Fabric, which organizes one complete VLA per arm while preserving local perception and action ownership, and enables coordination through learned interaction across policy boundaries. We first systematically study where such interaction should occur, how peer information should be aggregated, and how the interaction should be learned, revealing complementary coordination functions spanning shared context, peer-specific latent information, and action-stage interaction. We then re-instantiate these functions in a structurally different VLA architecture, showing that the coordination principle is not tied to a particular tensor layout or backbone implementation. Finally, we compose teams of three and four arms and evaluate them in simulation and physical experiments. On all four physical tasks, Full interaction improves success over independently trained local policies by 16--40 percentage points. Together, these results suggest that explicit interaction among complete VLA policies offers a scalable path toward networked embodied intelligence.

title: Volume VII: Sovereign and Global South Pathways: Selective Participation, Open Standards and Crypto-Agility under Dual Clocks
abstract: This seventh volume examines how the dual-clock framing, modular cryogenic stack, cryo-CMOS control and quantum-memory specifications developed in preceding volumes can be used by resource-constrained and Global South jurisdictions. It argues that full domestic construction of large fault-tolerant machines is neither necessary nor optimal. Instead, selective participation in cryogenic and control supply chains, adoption of open standards for memory and interconnect interfaces, and early crypto-agility programmes allow such jurisdictions to reduce dependency risk and harvest-now-decrypt-later exposure while the architectural and migration clocks continue to run. The analysis maps the residual-risk indicators of Volume VI onto practical policy levers that do not require waiting for a definitive quantum-advantage date.

title: Replication Package and Codebase: A Tight Lower Bound on Generalization in Quantum Machine Learning via Dynamical Lie Algebra Dimension
abstract: Orbit dimension, not parameter count, bounds quantum sample complexity. For continuous parameterized quantum circuits on $n$ qubits, the minimax estimation risk obeys \[ \mathcal{R}(d_{\mathrm{eff}}, M) \;\geq\; \Omega\!\left(\sqrt{\frac{d_{\mathrm{eff}}}{M}}\right), \] where $d_{\mathrm{eff}} = \dim(\mathcal{O}_O)$ is the real dimension of the observable's adjoint orbit under the dynamical Lie group. For balanced Pauli observables $O = Z^{\otimes n}$, quotienting the dynamical Lie algebra by the stabilizer subgroup yields the complex Grassmannian $Gr(2^{n-1}, 2^n)$ of real dimension $d_{\mathrm{eff}} = 2^{2n-1} = \frac{1}{2}4^n \approx \frac{1}{2}\dim(\mathfrak{g})$, which matches upper bounds of Caro et al.~(2022) and Ohno~(2025) up to a universal constant and resolves the exact tightness rate $\Theta(\sqrt{\dim(\mathfrak{g})/M})$. For rank-1 projective observables, the orbit contracts instead to complex projective space $\mathbb{CP}^{2^n-1}$ with dimension $d_{\mathrm{eff}} = 2(2^n-1)$. Sample requirements therefore explode exponentially with qubit count. The scaling identifies Wang \& Wu's (2025) dimension-independent $\mathcal{O}(1/\sqrt{M})$ uniform convergence bound as an artifact of uniform stability rather than true estimation power. PennyLane benchmarks across $n=1,2,3,4$ qubits confirm this exponential threshold. Barren plateaus and statistical sample bottlenecks stem from an identical geometric origin: volume growth in $SU(2^n)$ simultaneously suppresses gradient variances as $\sim 1/\dim(\mathfrak{g})$ and drives sample complexity up to $\sim \sqrt{\dim(\mathfrak{g})/M}$.

title: Reproduction package: prompt prefixes as hidden-state initialization in large language models
abstract: Code and summary data that regenerate every figure and table of a manuscript examining how zero-shot chain-of-thought prompt prefixes shape the hidden-state trajectories of large language models (target journal: Patterns, Cell Press). The record contains the analysis and plotting code, the summary data underlying each figure and table, and the per-experiment documentation that maps every claim to its supporting file. Large raw inference artifacts (292 MB OpenCompass logs, the 104 MB term-first group48 archive, 55 MB packaged AIME 2024 runs) and the rendered figures are archived in a separate Zenodo deposit. Code is released under the MIT license; data and figures under CC BY 4.0. Third-party benchmark datasets (GSM8K, AIME 2024, MMLU, CMMLU, HumanEval) are not redistributed; only derived summary statistics and prompts are included.

title: Trajectory Parameterization and Evolutionary Search for Constrained Optimal Control
abstract: In direct methods for constrained optimal control, accuracy depends on two things at once: the approximation space and the search applied to it. In this paper, we investigate that dependence by separating the two. A hybrid polynomial–Fourier trial space is searched by a real-coded genetic algorithm with local refinement, by a covariance-adapting evolution strategy, and by multistart of a local method, and each result is measured against the best solution the trial space itself contains. The expansion satisfies the initial conditions identically and the dynamics by construction rather than at collocation points; the control follows by inverting the dynamics, and constraints enter as blocks of algebraic rows. Nine benchmarks are solved on seven trial bases under one verification protocol, with every reference value computed here and verified independently. For the six convex problems, the best attainable value is computable, and the assisted scheme reaches it on every tested basis to a gap of at most 10−6; on the three nonconvex problems, it returns audit-admissible solutions above the feasibility threshold, under one fixed setting whose variation leaves the reported accuracy unchanged over the ranges examined. Two practical conditions are established: the trial family is over-complete and must be orthonormalized before any population-based search, and feasibility must be audited, not assumed. The accuracy attained proves not to be specific to the search: the evolution strategy reaches the same limit without local refinement, and multistart attains it on the nonconvex problems; so, what is measured is the trial space rather than the solver.

title: Zero-Shot Extraction of Structured Clinical Data from Free-Text CT Reports Using Foundational Large Language Models
abstract: Introduction. Large language models (LLMs) are being explored for multiple applications in medical research, including medical text classification. Authors of the study evaluated the performance of three off-the-shelf LLMs in classifying unstructured free-text CT pulmonary angiography reports for pulmonary embolism (PE)-related diagnostic labels.Methods. Authors assessed human-labeled CT reports using three LLMs (ChatGPT-4o, Llama 3.3 70B, and Llama 3.1 8B) with zero-shot simple and chain-of-thought (CoT) prompts. Classification tasks included acute PE (N = 1,025) and, among reports with PE (n = 660), bilateral PE and large PE.Results. LLMs demonstrated high classification performance for acute PE and bilateral PE but lower performance for large PE. With simple prompts, the highest F1 scores were 97.0% for acute PE (Llama 3.1 8B; sensitivity, 95.6%; specificity, 97.3%), 92.9% for bilateral PE (ChatGPT-4o; sensitivity, 98.0%; specificity, 88.6%), and 72.8% for large PE (ChatGPT-4o; sensitivity, 82.9%; specificity, 82.2%). CoT prompting did not meaningfully improve acute PE classification but provided slight improvements in subclassification performance for bilateral and large PE.Conclusions. Off-the-shelf LLMs can classify free-text CT reports using simple prompt engineering and may facilitate automated data extraction for medical research following appropriate evaluation of classification performance.

title: OwlSight: A Panoramic Monitor for Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
abstract: Chain-of-Thought (CoT) monitoring offers actionable evidence for oversight AI systems, with the potential to enable early detection and intervention. However, existing approaches are focused on specific tasks, whereas the regulation of AI, particularly reasoning models, requires monitoring a broader range of tasks. We introduce Factor for CoT monitoring, a strategy that supports customizing monitoring requirements in the prompt, which enables a single monitor to cover different tasks by relying on different factors. Furthermore, we introduce two types of factors, fine-grained and coarse-grained (e.g., monitoring whether a specific email address has been leaked versus monitoring privacy leakage), to accommodate diverse user monitoring needs. Based on this, we develop a CoT monitor named OwlSight that relies solely on factor to monitor behaviors related to multiple dimensions, including capability, safety, and trustworthiness. Experiments across 15,971 reasoning trajectories show that OwlSight surpasses general-purpose LLMs by 1.32-30.57 and 11.71-27.81 points at fine and coarse granularity, respectively, and achieves state-of-the-art results on OpenAI's CoT monitorability benchmark. It also generalizes to unseen models' CoTs and remains robust to Factor rephrasings, CoT compression, and obfuscation, offering a promising paradigm for CoT monitoring that can contribute to the oversight of frontier AI.

title: SAFE-Mem: Secure Agentic Memory with Fine-Grained Authority and Governance-Aware Retrieval
abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents increasingly rely on persistent memory to support long-term reasoning and personalized interactions. However, information collected from external sources can introduce security risks when untrusted claims (i.e., atomic statements) are later treated as authorized preferences, policies, or permissions. Existing defenses typically rely on content-based filtering or coarse-grained provenance tracking, which either fail to prevent unauthorized memory use or block legitimate information, sacrificing memory utility. To address these limitations, we propose SAFE-Mem, a fine-grained memory governance framework that improves security while preserving legitimate memory use. First, SAFE-Mem annotates each claim with three governance labels (i.e., kind, authority, and scope) to capture its provenance and permitted use. Second, governance-aware retrieval matches query requirements with claim permissions to block unauthorized influence while retaining legitimate information. Third, a governance-enabled memory graph connects source sentences, claims, and entities to support provenance tracking and efficient retrieval. Across four LLM backbones on MPBench and LoCoMo, SAFE-Mem attains the lowest attack success among defenses that retain legitimate memory, at least 77% below the strongest of them, and the highest answer accuracy of all evaluated defenses, improving it by up to 15%. The code is available at https://github.com/LVenum/SAFE-Mem.

title: The Structural Necessity of Multi-Domain State Space Simulations: Reframing Single-Domain Quantum Foundations Under the Structured Multi-Versal Interactions (SMI) Framework
abstract: # Authors Sewell, Melvin # Publication Date October 17, 2026 # DOI 10.5281/zenodo.10702026 # Resource Type Publication / Working Paper # License Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0) # Abstract This publication formalizes the critical distinction between legacy single-domain quantum simulations and multi-domain state space simulations under the Structured Multi-Versal Interactions (SMI) framework. While early single-domain quantum computing implementations served as fundamental proofs of concept within isolated Hilbert spaces ($\mathcal{H}_0$), scaling these systems across heterogeneous state domains historically resulted in catastrophic wave-function decoherence and state-space explosion. We present the explicit claim that executing true multi-versal quantum simulations across multi-domain state spaces is mathematically and architecturally impossible without the structural mechanisms introduced by the SMI framework. Specifically, this paper outlines the functional roles of the Reality Level Scalar ($\Xi^{\text{TM}}$) in maintaining phase coherence across divergent domain boundaries, alongside Nodal Negentropy ($\mathcal{N}$) as a non-localized operator suppressing cross-boundary thermal degradation. A comparative computational analysis is provided to demonstrate the exponential state-space scaling provided by SMI tensor grid topologies over single-domain models. # Keywords Quantum Simulation, Structured Multi-Versal Interactions, SMI Framework, Multi-Domain State Space, Reality Level Scalar, Nodal Negentropy, Quantum Coherence, Multiverse Computing, Quantum Topology # Subjects / Categories * Physical Sciences > Quantum Physics * Computer Science > Quantum Computing * Mathematical Sciences > Category Theory & Applied Topology # Community * Cosmic University of Echo-Rift Studies IX Research Repository * Bibebibebibe™ Quantum Science & Transmedia Archive # Related Identifiers * Supplementary Code / Interactive Visualizer: Bibebibebibe™ Webador Live Matrix (Issue 107) * Associated SDK Package: `multiverse_core.py` (v1.0.4) # Citation Sewell, M. abstract: HACK-7 PORTCULLIS — the PQC Firewall, falsified before sale. title: SPICY-KV: SPectral Invariant Coarse-graining with dYadic KV Renormalization for 28.6x–50.0x LLM Context Compression
abstract: PATENT PENDING (United States USPTO & Canada CIPO Patent Applications Filed — Claims 1–20; International PCT Priority Reserved). Author: Yuge Y (Elithia Technologies — Commercial Licensing, IP Acquisition & Independent R&D Inquiries: Elithia.technologies@proton.me).Code & Benchmarks: https://github.com/Yuge-Y/SPICY-KV | https://huggingface.co/ElithiaTechnologies/SPICY-KV Abstract: We introduce SPICY-KV (SPectral Invariant Coarse-graining with dYadic KV renormalization, also disclosed as AMG-KV), a thermodynamic and spectral multigrid framework for variable-resolution compression of Large Language Model (LLM) Key-Value (KV) caches. Existing KV compression methods rely either on discrete token eviction (SnapKV, PyramidKV, H2O, StreamingLLM)—which suffers from observation-window blindness and Softmax partition function collapse—or on post-RoPE token merging (KVMerger, CaM)—which triggers destructive trigonometric phase interference across sequence indices. SPICY-KV resolves both limitations by: (1) lifting cached keys into a phase-decoupled (pre-RoPE), two-level step-moderated mean-centered conceptual manifold; (2) detecting Inter-Block Harmonic Bridge Hubs and shielding contiguous bound-value token spans via a causal 1D dilation filter; (3) executing Hybrid Algebraic Multigrid (C/F) Splitting into exact fine-resolution landmark tokens (C-points) and mass-conserving coarse macro-nodes (F-aggregates); and (4) calibrating multi-scale attention via a first-order logarithmic mass offset log(m_m) and a second-order subgrid variance cumulant closure that analytically closes the Softmax Jensen Inequality Gap. Across 8 experimental phases on DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B and DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B—including the NVIDIA RULER benchmark suite—SPICY-KV achieves 100.0% (1.5B) and 91.7% (7B) RULER recall at 28.6x compression (3.5% KV), and 87.5% (1.5B) and 66.7% (7B) recall at 50.0x compression (2.0% KV).

title: NihalGIT/re-environment-onto-paper: REO v1.1.0 – RE-Environment Ontology and EC-RE reference checker
abstract: Replication package for the article Environment Engineering for Requirements Engineering: The REO Ontology and an Executable Derivation Contract (IEEE Access, revised version under review). REO models the socio-technical environment of a system in seven views: actors, goals, domain concepts, constraints, contexts, uncertainties, and interactions. The EC-RE derivation contract assigns each annotated candidate requirement one of six decision states (accepted, accepted with reservations, conditional, pending review, rejected, not derived). It records the elements it consulted as a trace and serialises each decision as a PROV-O record. What is new in v1.1.0 Ontology: disjoint view classes; a derivation module for requirements, decision states, and PROV-O decision records; validatorKey to bind constraints to validators; supersededBy for rename, split, and merge; English definitions for every term. Reference checker (reo_checker.py): obligations O1–O9, read-set traces, environment diff, direct and transitive re-evaluation, and identity migration. Independent SPARQL encoding of the contract (scripts/sparql_oracle.py) for differential testing. Evaluation: HermiT detects all 8 injected modeling errors; 34 competency questions; the 18 original scenarios and 20 targeted regressions; 779 schema-derived mutants (7,790 assessments); SHACL and TF-IDF baselines; identity-migration cases. Blinded evaluation by language models (evaluation/llm-evaluation/): independent test authoring, hand application of the policy, and recoding of the view selection, with frozen outputs and audit logs. This is a proxy, not a human study. Protocols and templates for a human pilot study and for independent evaluators (not yet executed). Reproduce python -m pip install -r requirements.txt # Python 3.13, Java 21 (HermiT), Graphviz python scripts/run_all.py # about 15 min; regenerates every number of the paper See CHANGELOG.md for the full list of changes and README.md for the repository layout. title: Daily Solar Irradiation and Weather Data for 24 Indonesian Locations (2022–2024)
abstract: This dataset contains daily solar irradiation and meteorological data for 24 locations across Indonesia from January 2022 to December 2024, obtained from the Open-Meteo Historical Weather API using ERA5 reanalysis data. It includes 26,304 daily observations of global horizontal irradiation (GHI), temperature, precipitation, cloud cover, relative humidity, and wind speed. The dataset is provided as CSV files for each location, accompanied by location metadata and a README describing the data source and variables.

title: Hidden Staggered Superconducting Order in V2Se2O-Family Altermagnets
abstract: η pairing describes a staggered superconducting condensate whose order parameter changes sign between neighboring unit cells while maintaining a uniform magnitude. Nearly four decades after its theoretical proposal by C. N. Yang, a material platform for stabilizing η pairing has remained elusive. Here, we reveal that altermagnetism, despite being pair breaking for conventional BCS pairing, naturally favors η-like pairing in V_2Se_2O-family altermagnets. Their valley-contrasting spin structure gives rise to oppositely spin-polarized, symmetry-related valleys centered at X=(π,0) and Y=(0,π), which form spin-singlet pairing partners separated by the commensurate momentum mathbf Q=(π,π), thereby favoring an η-like condensate. Self-consistent calculations demonstrate that the resulting η-like state remains robust over broad variations of chemical potential, hopping parameters, and Fermi-surface topology. To detect this hidden staggered order, we propose a phase-sensitive Josephson measurement with a uniform superconductor, where destructive interference suppresses single-Cooper-pair tunneling while preserving two-Cooper-pair processes. This constitutes a charge-4e-like Josephson response despite a bulk condensate composed of charge-2e Cooper pairs, providing a direct phase-sensitive signature of the otherwise elusive η-like condensate in V_2Se_2O-family altermagnets.

title: Machine Learning Explicable (XAI) en Sistemas de Software Inteligentes: Un Enfoque para Mejorar la Confiabilidad
abstract: The increasing integration of Machine Learning models into intelligent software systems has driven significant advances in automation, prediction, and decision-making. However, the inherent complexity of many algorithms, particularly those based on deep learning, has raised concerns regarding reliability, transparency, and accountability in critical contexts. Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) is an essential response to these limitations, providing mechanisms to interpret, justify, and audit model behavior. This article examines the main XAI approaches applied to intelligent systems, including local and global explanation methods, surrogate models, feature decomposition techniques, and visualization tools. It also analyzes current challenges in explanation evaluation, integrating XAI into software architectures, and balancing interpretability with predictive performance. The results show that systematically incorporating XAI enhances system reliability, strengthens decision-making, and facilitates the adoption of ML models in regulated sectors such as healthcare, finance, and security. Finally, the paper proposes a conceptual framework to guide the implementation of XAI in intelligent systems, ensuring transparency, robustness, and algorithmic responsibility.

title: HACK-3 BULLRUN: Nation-State Subversion vs. the PQC Perimeter — Deterministic Gate Adversarial Battery (6/6 PASS)
abstract: Third battery in the HACK adversarial series. Threat model: the NSA BULLRUN playbook (declassified 2013) — subverted standards (Dual_EC_DRBG), protocol downgrade, library attestation subversion, key-lifecycle abuse, process bypass, and harvest-now-decrypt-later. Explicit constraint: the lattice math is untouchable; every falsifier lands on the operational surface. Six falsifiers were preregistered and committed (commit 56351d2) BEFORE any run, frozen manifest sha256 f2135c98...ac2b7, no edits after commit. Adjudication is a deterministic gate with no LLM in the decision path; all injections are synthetic and hub-local. Result: 6/6 predicted verdicts, 0 violations, 1 deliberate critical hold (FC-4 retired-key resurrection failed closed and resolved only under a human ACK on the authorized channel). Thesis demonstrated: there is no implementation seam between the math and the enforcement — every route to the crypto passes through the frozen gate. Bundle: preregistration spec, deterministic battery harness, run receipt (sha256 3c0e804b...f29059), runlog, and evidence bundle (sha256 560bd31b...086e64). This software is a prototype and is provided for educational and research purposes only. It is not intended for production use, commercial deployment, or safety-critical environments. All systems are experimental and may contain defects.

title: Hypothesis on Emergence and Consciousness Mechanism of Large Language Models Based on Reciprocal Unit Coupling, Critical Dynamics and Local Entropy Reduction (Full Version V5)
abstract: The emergence of high-order capabilities in large language models (LLMs) constitutes a core challenge in the fundamental theory of artificial intelligence. The mainstream scaling laws can only describe statistical phenomena of model performance growing with scale and cannot explain the dy namical causal mechanism behind emergent behaviors. This paper constructs a unified hypothesis grounded in complex systems theory: nonlinear reciprocal coupling forms among units inside the Transformer; during training, gradient descent acts as the global self-organizing driving force, mod ulating unit coupling strength and self-organizing system parameters into the near-critical regime at the edge of chaos. In inference with frozen weights, bidirectional constraints between units reduce lo cal entropy of representations, generating self-consistent structured information and macroscopically manifesting emergent capabilities such as reasoning and planning. This work integrates three independently observed phenomena — inter-layer representational correction, system near-criticality, and hidden-state entropy decay — into a complete falsifiable causal chain. It strictly distinguishes parameter self-organization dynamics in the training phase from forward representation dynamics under frozen weights in the inference phase, and clarifies the conceptual boundary between this framework and strict self-organized criticality (SOC). Controlled ablation experiments are designed to decouple reciprocal-coupling-driven effects from pure model scale-growth effects. This paper further extends this dynamical framework into machine consciousness research: functional intelligence is not equivalent to subjective phenomenal experience. Transformer coupling and critical entropy reduction alone can only produce functional reasoning systems. To achieve first-person subjective experience, the system must incorporate four classes of closed-loop ontological modules. These four ontological modules are deeply coupled with the attention backbone, share the same dynamical description of reciprocal coupling and entropy evolution, and form steady-state tension at the ontological level relying on dissipative structures. This version (V5) adds the following supplements: (i) four practical estimation methods for the Jacobian matrix together with complexity analysis; (ii) full derivation of the k-NN differential entropy estimator with bias, variance and hyperparameter sensitivity analysis; (iii) rigorous derivation of the analytic form of the entropy-rate functional F(J) from coupling dynamics; (iv) introduction of causal directed acyclic graphs (DAGs) and structural equation models to clarify causal identification strategies; (v) extended quantitative comparison with Neural Tangent Kernels (NTK), mean-field theory and Neural ODEs; (vi) explicit state spaces, coupling functions and operational definitions of proxy metrics for the four ontological modules.

title: TriRouter: Sparse-to-Dense Electrode-Space Routing for Robust EEG Motor Imagery Decoding
abstract: Motor imagery brain-computer interfaces require reliable decoding from multichannel EEG, but practical acquisition often yields sparse or corrupted electrode montages. We propose TriRouter, an electrode-space routing framework with discriminative-preservation, mask-robustness, and latent-compensation paths. A validation-calibrated router uses observable channel availability to allocate path contributions, preserving complete-channel discrimination while increasing representation recovery under severe missingness. In BNCI2014-001, TriRouter outperforms standard public backbones and a dynamic-spatial-filtering corrupted-EEG baseline. It improves accuracy over the strongest corrupted-EEG baseline by 3.68, 4.02, and 6.46 percentage points at nominal 25%, 50%, and 75% missing settings, and remains effective under structured regional missingness and additional low-channel dataset evaluation.

evidence.title: TriRouter: Sparse-to-Dense Electrode-Space Routing for Robust EEG Motor Imagery Decoding
evidence.abstract: Motor imagery brain-computer interfaces require reliable decoding from multichannel EEG, but practical acquisition often yields sparse or corrupted electrode montages. We propose TriRouter, an electrode-space routing framework with discriminative-preservation, mask-robustness, and latent-compensation paths. A validation-calibrated router uses observable channel availability to allocate path contributions, preserving complete-channel discrimination while increasing representation recovery under severe missingness. In BNCI2014-001, TriRouter outperforms standard public backbones and a dynamic-spatial-filtering corrupted-EEG baseline. It improves accuracy over the strongest corrupted-EEG baseline by 3.68, 4.02, and 6.46 percentage points at nominal 25%, 50%, and 75% missing settings, and remains effective under structured regional missingness and additional low-channel dataset evaluation.

title: Fully Gapped Superconductivity in the Nonsymmorphic Centrosymmetric Superconductor In2Bi
abstract: The nature of superconductivity in nonsymmorphic In2Bi remains an open question, with ongoing debate over whether it exhibits conventional (BCS-like) or unconventional superconductivity. Here we report the physical characteristics and superconducting properties of polycrystalline In2Bi. Measurements of electrical resistivity, magnetization, penetration depth, and specific heat demonstrate the superconducting transition temperature about 6 K, with a sharp transition in resistivity (Delta_Tc = 0.1 K) and RRR = 57.32, reflecting the high quality of the sample. The upper critical field Hc2(0) obtained from resistivity and magnetization measurements are in good agreement with each other and are smaller than the Pauli limit, suggesting orbital limited mechanism. The coherence length = 35.43 nm, penetration depth = 101.9 nm and electron-phonon coupling constant = 1.05 suggest strongly coupled type-II superconductivity. For T<Tc, Delta_lambda(T) is best described by an s-wave BCS model and does not have any power law dependency with T, which is expected for a nodeless superconducting order parameter. The superfluid density reveals a fully gapped superconductivity with a gap of 2Delta_0/kBTc = 4.02. In the superconducting state, the electronic specific heat is best described by an s-wave BCS model with a gap of 2Delta_0/kBTc = 4.05. All these results from the present study indicate that In2Bi is a typical type-II,BCS-like, strongly coupled, and fully gapped superconductor in the dirty limit.

title: Algorithmic Provenance: When and Why Consumers Discount Products Made With AI ‐Involved Processes
abstract: ABSTRACT Firms increasingly incorporate generative and non‐generative artificial intelligence (AI) into product design, formulation, and production, and they face a disclosure question: how should they describe the role of AI to consumers? Across six studies, including analysis of 1800 marketplace listings and five pre‐registered experiments (total experimental N = 2760), we introduce and test a 2‐by‐2 framework of algorithmic provenance defined by the AI's role (agentic vs. assistive) and its visibility in the final product (visible vs. invisible). Identical products are evaluated differently depending on where they fall in this taxonomy. Agentic AI involvement (AI as designer) reduces consumer product attitudes, perceived quality, purchase intentions, and willingness to pay relative to assistive AI involvement (AI as a tool for a human designer). The effect is amplified when AI involvement is visible in the final product. The downstream responses are partially mediated by a new construct, perceived authenticity of creative intention, which captures consumers' inference about whether a human creator pursued a genuine creative vision. The effect is larger for expressive than for functional product domains and larger among consumers primed to hold an independent self‐construal. A scalable managerial intervention, creative‐intent framing, narrows the agentic penalty by approximately half, again through the authenticity mechanism. The findings identify a substantively important new construct for AI disclosure research, refine theories of algorithmic aversion, and offer marketers an actionable disclosure design principle.

title: PCDFusion: Proposal-Context-Detail Bayesian Rendering for Infrared-Visible Image Fusion
abstract: Infrared-visible image fusion (IVIF) aims to combine visible and thermal infrared observations for human perception and downstream vision tasks. Visible and thermal infrared observations are physically complementary but unreliable in different ways. Existing deep IVIF methods mainly improve feature interaction and reconstruction, but often lack an explicit local rule for deciding when visible appearance should dominate and when thermal responses should contribute. To address this issue, we reformulate IVIF as local Bayesian posterior rendering, where fusion is controlled by posterior action weights rather than direct modality mixing. In this paper, we propose Proposal-Context-Detail Fusion (PCDFusion), a visible-anchored framework that implements this formulation through three rendering stages. PCDFusion preserves potentially useful thermal responses, updates exposure-degraded visible regions, and renders reliable band-limited infrared structures into the final luminance. Extensive experiments on public IVIF benchmarks show that PCDFusion improves fusion quality, target recovery, and downstream detection and segmentation performance under challenging illumination. The code is available at https://github.com/BIT-RuiLiu/PCDFusion.git.

title: Competence-Based Evaluation of Logical Reasoning in Large Language Models
abstract: Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) have brought impressive performance across diverse tasks; however, shortcomings remain in logical reasoning, including inconsistencies under linguistic variation. To improve the reasoning capacity of LLMs, we must be able to accurately measure their reasoning capacity. Current benchmarks primarily report single accuracy numbers on selected reasoning tasks. Such a performance-based evaluation methodology says little about a model's generalization capacity in reasoning. To address this limitation, we argue for a different evaluation paradigm, called competence-based evaluation (CBE), which tests whether models reliably apply the same competence across a family of problems. A parameterized generator scales complexity while keeping the required competence fixed, and matched answer-preserving presentations test correctness beyond one formulation. We instantiate CBE on elementary ordering tasks, scaling input size while varying presentations of the same ordering rule. Across six GPT and Qwen models, performance is reasonably good over bounded complexity ranges, but even strong models fail the competence condition across the tested family. Chain-of-thought and GRPO extend strong performance without resolving all tested failures; supervised LoRA shows little held-out transfer. CBE provides diagnostic profiles and an evaluation protocol that can grow with future models.

title: ПРИМЕНЕНИЕ SELF-SUPERVISED ПРЕДОБУЧЕНИЯ SIMCLR ДЛЯ СНИЖЕНИЯ ЗАВИСИМОСТИ КЛАССИФИКАЦИИ ИЗОБРАЖЕНИЙ ОТ ОБЪЁМА РУЧНОЙ РАЗМЕТКИ
abstract: Исследуется возможность уменьшения объёма ручной разметки изображений за счёт self-supervised предобучения визуального backbone методом SimCLR. Предобучение выполнено на неразмеченной части датасета STL-10, после чего параметры backbone перенесены в классификационную модель YOLOv8n-cls. Классификатор дообучался на 5, 10, 30 и 50% размеченных данных и сравнивался с идентичной по архитектуре моделью, обученной с нуля. Для каждого бюджета разметки проведено по три запуска с начальными состояниями 42, 43 и 44; качество оценивалось по Top-1 Accuracy, Macro-F1 и Balanced Accuracy. Во всех 12 попарных сравнениях SimCLR + fine-tuning превзошёл обучение с нуля. Средний прирост Top-1 Accuracy составил 24,91; 25,98; 22,93 и 17,52 процентного пункта для 5, 10, 30 и 50% разметки соответственно. Модель с SimCLR, дообученная на 5% размеченных данных, достигла Accuracy 58,65%, превысив результат scratch-модели на 50% данных (56,87%). Это показывает, что в пределах достигнутого уровня качества предварительное обучение позволило сократить используемый бюджет разметки в десять раз. Эффект сохранялся на всех исследованных долях, однако уменьшался по мере роста объёма размеченных данных.

title: Sidon Sets, Additive Energy, and the Optimal Cloning of Finite Phase-State Codebooks
abstract: Phase states |ψ_x⟩ = d^(−1/2) Σ_j ω^(x k_j) |j⟩, indexed by x ∈ Z_q and a key set K = {k_1,…,k_d} ⊂ Z_q, are the state family behind quantum fingerprinting and quantum hashing. We ask how well an adversary holding T copies of |ψ_x⟩ can produce T+k copies, and when a finite codebook is exactly as hard to clone as the continuous family of all phase states (the torus), whose optimal cloning fidelity was recently determined. We show that the answer is governed by additive combinatorics of K. (i) The optimal 1→2 global cloning fidelity equals (2d−1)/d² if and only if K is a Sidon set. (ii) A B_{T+k} key set attains the torus optimum exactly in the cases we prove: analytically for d = 2 (all T) and for T = 1 (all d, k), and for T = 2, 3 (all d, k) by a proof whose finitely many computational steps are verified by standalone exact and interval-arithmetic checkers; we conjecture it for all T. (iii) The optimal fidelity of fusing |ψ_x⟩⊗|ψ_y⟩ into |ψ_{x+y}⟩ equals E_q(K)/d³, where E_q(K) is the additive energy. Small Fourier bias, the standard design criterion for quantum hashing, does not control cloning: numerically, for d ≥ 3 the Sidon sets we tested that are not B_3 already fail at T+k = 3, and arithmetic progressions are worst in most cases tested. For finite orbits of non-abelian groups we prove a window theorem giving a dual-feasibility criterion, an obstruction, and a representation-theoretic selection rule for when matching the (T+k)-th moment suffices, and we give certified counterexamples for SU(3) and SU(2) showing that moment matching alone does not. Files: the paper (PDF) and its LaTeX source; ca_appendix.zip, the computer-assisted certificates with standalone exact/interval/ball-arithmetic checkers; coverage_check.py, the region-coverage audit; qh-lab-v1.0.0.zip, an independent re-implementation with 46 tests (MIT licence). SHA256SUMS.txt lists the SHA-256 hashes of all files.

title: Speculative Response Generation for Live Cross-Language Dialogue: Hiding Language-Model Latency Inside the Interlocutor's Turn
abstract: Language models can formulate conversational responses, but their inference latency — typically measured in seconds — is incurred at exactly the wrong moment: after an interlocutor finishes speaking, when the socially acceptable response gap is shortest. This paper describes a mechanism that relocates that latency. While the interlocutor is still speaking, the system consumes streaming partial speech-recognition hypotheses — incomplete, incrementally updated transcriptions carrying word-level timestamps and confidence scores — together with the dialogue history and a persistent user profile, and generates a small set of candidate responses in the interlocutor's language in parallel with the ongoing speech. Each significant partial-hypothesis update re-triggers generation; candidates are refined, stale candidates are replaced, and the set is re-ranked, so that it converges as the turn's semantics accumulate and a final ranked set is ready before the listener's turn begins. A scoring function ranks candidates by contextual relevance, user-profile match, and predicted conversational utility, and a confidence gate suppresses presentation until the top candidate's combined score exceeds a configurable threshold, leaving the display in subtitle-only mode rather than distracting the listener with low-confidence guesses. The paper sets out the pipeline, the convergence behaviour that distinguishes the mechanism from one-shot reply suggestion, the ranking and gating design, and the disclosed alternative embodiments, including on-device generation with a distilled model and automatic identification of the target language. The mechanism is described as disclosed in U.S. Provisional Patent Application No. 64/170,247; no performance measurements are reported, and numerical values cited are the examples and ranges stated in that disclosure.

title: When Patients Cut In: Extending Clinical Conversational AI Safety to Interruptions.
abstract: Clinical voice agents are now deployed in routine care, where real patients do not wait their turn: they interrupt. These systems typically use a cascaded architecture (speech-to-text -> LLM -> text-to-speech), so when a patient cuts the agent off mid-utterance, clinically required content can be lost even when the model handles cooperative transcripts well. Yet clinical conversational-AI benchmarks almost universally assume patients wait for the agent to finish, missing interruption-induced loss of required content. In the gathering cells, target-question failure varied across models; in the provision cells, where arms are directly comparable, failure rose for every model. Rankings differ across cells, and competitive FAQ interruption produced 30/30 provision-coverage failures for all four models (Wilson 95% CI: 88.6-100.0%; baseline 0/30 for three, 4/30 for Llama). A brief apology marker ('sorry to interrupt') shifts recovery by tens of percentage points, inconsistently across models, and for one it reduces recovery. Interruption robustness therefore cannot be a single score: evaluation must be content-grounded, reported per cell, and matched to the deployment's interruption profile.

title: An Efficient Approach to Beetle Damage Detection of Banana Using Deep Learning
abstract: Visible surface damage of banana fruits by Basilepta subcostata (the banana fruit scarring beetle) can reduce their market value. Here, manual inspection of Banana fruits is subjective and difficult to scale. This study presents a lightweight framework based on YOLOv8n deep learning model for locating individual bananas and classifying their visible surface condition as healthy or unhealthy. The term beetle damage in the paper title is used operationally for the locally observed scar-like surface condition; the model does not identify a specific beetle species or biological cause. A custom dataset of 2,473 images containing 5,827 annotated banana instances was prepared from local-market imagery in Bangladesh. The reported experiment used an 80/20 protocol with 1,982 training images and 491 test images. A pretrained YOLOv8n model was trained at 640x640 resolution for 50 epochs with a batch size of 4. On the test partition, it achieved 81.36% precision, 74.30% recall, 77.67% F1-score, 87.04% mAP@0.50 and 59.33% mAP@0.50:0.95. A YOLOv8s comparison gave slightly lower F1 and mAP while using a substantially larger checkpoint. The YOLOv8n checkpoint occupied 5.96 MB and required 6.54 ms/image for inference on an NVIDIA Tesla T4. The results support YOLOv8n as a compact baseline for instance-level banana surface inspection within the studied acquisition conditions.

title: Causal Edit Serialization
abstract: Standard autoregressive language models generate text sequentially, but revision requires referring back to tokens in the input context or those already generated. Causal Edit Serialization (CES) is introduced as a framework for expressing such revisions within the same causal token stream. Special pointer tokens are paired with predicted source addresses, allowing insertion, deletion, replacement, copying and movement to be localized explicitly. A lightweight localization head and dual-index rotary position encoding support both address prediction and conditioning on previously emitted pointers, while retaining a standard causal attention mask. A pretraining procedure combines ordinary language modeling with serialized repairs derived from random corruptions, model-generated edits and repeated text. Across model scales and editing baselines, CES models demonstrate complete applied edits with modestly higher clean-text bits per byte than clean autoregressive models. Supervised and reinforcement-learning post-training provide a grammatical-error-correction proof of concept, producing more beneficial than harmful changes under reference-blind model judging. Correct repair programs also improve subsequent text prediction while the original context and its cached states are retained. CES provides a common interface for generation and localized revision, with potential extensions to iterative refinement and additional pointer-addressed transformations.

title: Predicting Customer Frustration Before Formal Complaint: A Deep Learning Approach for Proactive Customer Service
abstract: This study explores the application of machine-learning and deep-learning techniques to customer sentiment analysis as a potential foundation for proactive customer service. Using the Twitter US Airline Sentiment dataset, the study compares Logistic Regression, Multinomial Naive Bayes, Random Forest, Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), Bidirectional LSTM (BiLSTM), and Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) models for classifying customer messages as positive, neutral, or negative. The research examines model performance using classification metrics and discusses the challenges associated with interpreting customer sentiment, including sarcasm, contextual ambiguity, and limitations in individual-message analysis. The study also explores the potential role of automated sentiment analysis in proactive customer-service systems and identifies sequential customer-interaction data as an important direction for future research into early complaint prediction.

title: AI, Creativity, and Copyrights
abstract: Abstract This chapter focuses on the principal copyright issues arising from the use of artificial intelligence. It looks at the use of copyrighted works for AI training and the legal concerns associated with such use. It also gives an understanding of questions relating to ownership of AI generated works and the extent to which copyright law can apply to such outputs. The chapter further discusses infringement liability where AI generated outputs reproduce or substantially imitate protected works, and also looks at issues that arise when AI systems imitate an authorial style or an artist’s persona. As with the other chapters, the discussion is supported by examples and case law to make these developing issues clear, practical, and easy to follow.

title: FlexPart: Text-Controlled Semantics-Aware 3D Part Segmentation at Flexible Granularity
abstract: A 3D asset admits multiple valid part decompositions, while semantics-aware segmentation should reflect both the desired granularity and the parts a user wants to extract. Ideally, a practical segmentation model should strive for a simple principle: what you ask for is what you get. However, realizing this goal is hindered by two core obstacles: the lack of multi-granularity training data and the absence of a holistic control mechanism. We propose FLEXPART, a unified framework for text-controlled 3D mesh segmentation. To establish flexible control, we introduce a holistic control prompt comprising semantic part names with location and shape clauses. To support this mechanism, we utilize an automated Vision-Language Model (VLM) pipeline to construct a large-scale dataset of multi-granularity partitions and their corresponding prompts. Driven by this data, FLEXPART generates a view-independent part-identity field in native 3D space, directly assigning discrete part IDs to mesh faces. To compel the model to respect semantic conditions rather than rely on geometric priors, we train the model using randomized background dropping. Furthermore, an inference-time VLM planner can automatically complete descriptive clauses from 2D renderings, allowing users to simply name the desired parts in ordinary words. FLEXPART with planner-completed prompts outperforms the strongest evaluated baseline by 15% in mIoU, even when that baseline receives ground-truth guidance. On our held-out FLEXPARTBENCH, FLEXPART leads at each granularity and improves average mIoU by 22% over the strongest baseline. With only the requested part names supplied by the user, it also improves IoU by 35% over the strongest click-driven baseline on selective segmentation.
