title: Reasoning Reranking with Semantic IDs as the Sole Item Representation
abstract: Reasoning rerankers write a rationale before ranking a candidate slate, and existing systems read item metadata to do so, even though generative recommenders increasingly represent items as compact Semantic IDs (SIDs). Ranking from SIDs alone has two appeals: SID prompts are far shorter than the matched item text, and although item codes are fixed from content, the backbone learns their token embeddings in part from user-item interaction sequences, so the tokens can carry behavioral signal that item text lacks. That training targets next-item generation, and whether it supports ranking a supplied slate from SIDs alone is untested. We build ReRankID, a controlled testbed in which models reason and rank from a history and slate shown only as SIDs, varying item rendering, history length, and slate size one at a time. On this testbed, such models often copy the input order instead of reranking, and readable metadata does not repair the failure. We compare supervised fine-tuning, rejection-sampled self-training, on-policy distillation, and verifier-based reinforcement learning as post-training methods and find that they elicit the missing behavior. The strongest post-trained model, the 8B model trained with a graded ranking reward, gives the best SID-only ranking and matches strong text-reading LLMs whose prompts are about 20x longer. It ranks above random with no history at all, where a caption-reading reference does not, and it keeps its gains at long histories, where text prompts pass 50k tokens and the caption-reading reference stops improving. In a paired rationale audit, this model argues trade-offs better than that reference but describes items less accurately. The common post-training methods we test thus elicit ranking from SIDs but not faithful item descriptions, which calls for post-training that improves the reasoning itself, not only the ranking it produces.

title: Short-Term Solar Power Forecasting Based on Pruning-Optimized Temporal Convolutional Networks for Edge Deployment
abstract: Accurate multi-horizon solar power forecasting is vital for modern power distribution networks, yet standard deep learning models face limitations due to weather stochasticity and prohibitive computational requirements on resource-constrained edge devices. To address these issues, this paper proposes a Physics-Informed Similar-Day Data Augmentation (PI-SDDA) framework coupled with a Pruning-Optimized Temporal Convolutional Network (POTCN). The PI-SDDA strategy integrates multi-variable meteorological dynamics with candidate cluster size optimization to capture diurnal thermal periodicity and transient weather variations. To enable lightweight deployment, POTCN incorporates Batch Normalization scaling factors for channel-level sparsification within dilated causal residual blocks, significantly reducing parameter redundancy while preserving temporal receptive fields. Experimental results demonstrate superior forecasting performance across fifteen-minute, one-hour, and two-hour prediction horizons under standard statistical metrics compared with existing benchmarks. Edge hardware deployment tests on an embedded edge computing platform further verify low inference latency and minimal power consumption. The proposed framework provides an accurate, resource-efficient solution for real-time edge intelligence in power systems.

title: Self-Evolving Coding Agents via Harness-Policy Optimization
abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents have shown promising potential in coding tasks, and their performance is jointly determined by the policy model and the harness that mediates their interaction with the environment. Indeed, harness and policy are mutually reinforcing and evolving only one component is suboptimal---a harness tuned for one checkpoint may not target the failure modes of an updated policy, while policy learning remains limited to the trajectories elicited by a fixed harness. In light of this, we propose Self-HPO, a recursive self-improving framework for coding agents that alternates harness and policy optimization, using the evolving policy as its own harness proposer. Specifically, in each round, the current policy first analyzes its own failures and proposes new harness candidates (H-step). The policy is then updated through reinforcement learning (RL) under the selected harness (P-step), and hard tasks identified during training form the next harness search set, keeping harness optimization targeted to the policy's evolving failure modes. Across three coding benchmarks, Self-HPO consistently outperforms harness-only and policy-only baselines, improving Qwen3.5-35B-A3B's average resolve rate from 57.8% to 64.8%, with gains generalizing to out-of-distribution settings. Further analysis shows that both optimized components retain gains even when paired with their base counterparts, while their joint gain exceeds the sum of their individual gains. Self-HPO also improves reliability (Pass@1) and expands the capability frontier (Pass@k) over the base agent. Additionally, we show that with a stronger external model (e.g., Opus 4.8) as the harness proposer, the same framework yields a further performance boost.

title: ChronIQ-DRx2: restoring unwritten clinical decision logic unlocks personalized chronic disease management
abstract: Clinical records routinely document medical interventions but often omit the reasoning connecting patient-specific evidence to medical action. This limits the decision-relevant supervision available for training models for personalized care. Here we evaluate a data-augmentation approach that makes selected clinical decision relationships explicit in an 8-billion-parameter Qwen3 model, ChronIQ-DRx2. Using the same training cases and model architecture, expert-guided logic reconstruction was applied across four chronic diseases. On the held-out evaluation, the enhanced model had the highest plotted end-to-end task-completion rate among evaluated systems and higher plotted scores across diagnostic, medication and follow-up measures. The serious clinical error rates shown were 16.7% for the baseline and 12.5% for the enhanced model. In the human-AI evaluation, physician accuracy was 87.40% alone and 88.20% with AI assistance, while mean completion time was 0.959 and 0.780 min, respectively; medical-student accuracy was 62.71% and 74.80%, and mean completion time was 0.210 and 0.195 min. These results are descriptive point estimates; inferential comparisons are not reported here. Structured outputs may make recommendations easier to review, but rationale faithfulness, generalizability and effects on clinical safety require further evaluation.

title: O'ZBEK TILIDAGI TIBBIY HUJJATLAR KORPUSINI SHAKLLANTIRISH VA TIL MODELINI SOHAGA MOSLASHTIRISH METODOLOGIYASI
abstract: Annotatsiya. Ushbu maqolada o‘zbek tilidagi tibbiy hujjatlar (kasallik tarixi, epikriz, retsept va boshqa klinik matnlar) asosida maxsuslashtirilgan matn korpusini shakllantirish hamda transformer arxitekturasiga asoslangan til modelini (BERT/GPT tipidagi) ushbu sohaga moslashtirish metodologiyasi ko‘rib chiqiladi. Tibbiy matnlarning o‘ziga xos leksik-grammatik xususiyatlari, ularni yig‘ish va tanlash mezonlari, shaxsiy ma’lumotlarni anonimlashtirish tamoyillari, matnlarni me’yorlashtirish (normalizatsiya) bosqichlari, shuningdek tayanch modelni tanlash va tokenizatorni sohaviy leksikaga moslashtirish masalalari tahlil qilinadi. Kalit so‘zlar: tabiiy tilni qayta ishlash, tibbiy matnlar korpusi, transformer modellari, BERT, GPT, anonimlashtirish, tokenizatsiya, sohaga moslashtirish, o‘zbek tili. Аннотация. В статье рассматривается методология создания специализированного корпуса текстов на основе медицинских документов на узбекском языке (историй болезни, эпикризов, рецептов и других клинических текстов) и адаптации языковой модели на базе архитектуры трансформер (например, BERT или GPT) к данной предметной области. Анализируются специфические лексико-грамматические характеристики медицинских текстов, критерии их сбора и отбора, принципы анонимизации персональных данных, этапы нормализации текстов, а также вопросы выбора базовой модели и адаптации токенизатора к отраслевой лексике. Ключевые слова: обработка естественного языка, корпус медицинских текстов, трансформерные модели, BERT, GPT, анонимизация, токенизация, адаптация к предметной области, узбекский язык. Abstract. This article examines the methodology for creating a specialized text corpus based on medical documents in the Uzbek language (medical histories, epicrises, prescriptions, and other clinical texts) and for adapting a transformer-based language model (such as BERT or GPT) to this domain. It analyzes the specific lexical-grammatical characteristics of medical texts, criteria for their collection and selection, principles of personal data anonymization, stages of text normalization, as well as issues regarding the selection of a base model and the adaptation of the tokenizer to domain-specific vocabulary. Keywords: natural language processing, medical text corpus, transformer models, BERT, GPT, anonymization, tokenization, domain adaptation, Uzbek language.

title: ALEX-GWO: Reinforcement-learning-driven Adaptive Grey Wolf Optimization with Landscape-aware Local-optima Escape for Large-scale Global Optimization
abstract: Large-scale global optimization exposes a structural weakness of the grey wolf optimizer: its convergence coefficient follows a schedule fixed in advance, the three leading wolves collapse into a single attraction basin long before the budget is spent, and that loss of diversity is neither detected nor repaired.Published variants answer the symptoms with fixed remedies applied on a schedule rather than on evidence, so their cost is paid whether or not the population is trapped.This paper presents ALEX-GWO (Adaptive Learning-driven EXploration Grey Wolf Optimizer), which closes the loop between observation and control.A six-component search-state vector summarises progress, diversity, success rate, improvement, stagnation and leader dispersion; population-level parameter control, per-wolf success memory and an epsilon-greedy Q-learning selector consume it at three time scales; and a composite landscapetrapping score releases a targeted escape only when several independent indicators agree.On CEC'2013 and CEC'2010 at 1000 dimensions under an equal budget of 3.0 x 10^6 evaluations, ALEX-GWO obtains the best average Friedman rank of the ten algorithms compared on the first suite (2.00) and of the nine on the second (1.85)a set including ADSL-GWO, RL-LGWO and IAGWO re-implemented under an identical protocoland improves on canonical GWO by a median of four orders of magnitude.It reaches a lower mean error than SHADE-ILS on 13 of the 15 CEC'2013 functions (Wilcoxon p = 0.048) but is not separated from MOS, CC-RDG3 or IAGWO after Holm correction, so the evidence supports competitive consistency rather than dominance.ALEX-GWO costs 11.3% more runtime than canonical GWO, and removing landscape detection alone drops the escape success rate from 0.68 to 0.31.A binary variant reaches 90.32-93.75%accuracy under nested cross-validation on four feature-selection datasets while discarding 65-97% of the features.Code and raw results: https://github.com/Rajpreet-kaur1989/ALEXGWO.

title: Achieving lightweight policy-hiding access control and efficient auditing for IoT-based electronic health records in the cloud
abstract: The widespread adoption of Internet of Things (IoT) technologies in healthcare has led to the continuous generation of Electronic Health Records (EHRs) that are often outsourced to cloud storage. While cloud platforms offer scalability and availability, they introduce significant challenges in enforcing fine-grained access control, preserving policy privacy, and supporting efficient public auditing over large volumes of IoT-generated data. Existing solutions mainly focus on access authorization and provide limited support for scalable and privacy-preserving auditing. This paper proposes SEC-HIoT , a secure and efficient access control framework for IoT-based EHR systems. Rather than attempting to remove bilinear pairings from ciphertext-policy attribute-based encryption (CP-ABE), which the recent cryptanalysis of pairing-free constructions shows to be unsafe, SEC-HIoT confines them: encryption performs no pairing at all, and the pairings needed for decryption are executed by the fog against a blinded transformation key, so no pairing is ever computed on a resource-constrained device. To protect access policies, the scheme employs a secret-keyed attribute encoding mechanism that achieves attribute-label hiding against dictionary attacks, and the same encoding makes the construction usable over efficient asymmetric pairings. User revocation is handled by a lightweight perturbable mechanism that updates only the ciphertext blinding component and the keys of users who remain authorised, leaving the encrypted payload untouched. For auditing, SEC-HIoT combines Bloom filter–based indexing with Merkle tree verification to enable fast record lookup and lightweight integrity checking, while a blockchain-backed randomized signature mechanism supports both public auditing and owner-resolvable accountability without exposing signer identities. Security analysis establishes confidentiality, unforgeability, attribute-label hiding, and backward secrecy under revocation. A working implementation shows that the device-side decryption cost is independent of policy size at \(\approx \bf 2.3\) ms, a \(\bf 261\times\) reduction over the non-outsourced path at fifty attributes, that the IoT device performs no public-key operation during ingest, and that revoking a user costs a single group exponentiation per record instead of re-encryption.

title: Globally guided multi-agent reinforcement learning with decoupled critics for cooperative UAV path planning
abstract: Abstract Cooperative path planning for multiple unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) requires the simultaneous achievement of target navigation, collision avoidance, and formation coordination in complex obstacle environments. Existing multi-agent reinforcement learning methods often suffer from sparse rewards, local deadlocks, and conflicts between formation maintenance and obstacle avoidance, which can destabilize policy learning. To address these issues, this paper proposes a Globally Guided Decoupled-Critic Multi-Agent Soft Actor-Critic algorithm (GDC-MASAC). RRT $$^*$$ -based global guidance provides reference waypoints for the leader UAV, reducing inefficient exploration and local deadlocks. Three decoupled Critic branches separately evaluate target navigation, formation maintenance, and safety objectives, while an environment-aware formation reward adjustment relaxes formation tracking near obstacles according to the distance to obstacle boundaries. Experiments under different obstacle densities and swarm sizes show that GDC-MASAC improves mission completion, collision avoidance, and formation coordination. In a scenario with 12 obstacles and 3 UAVs, GDC-MASAC achieves a mission success rate of 86%, whereas the baseline methods achieve success rates below 50%. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of GDC-MASAC for cooperative multi-UAV path planning in cluttered environments.

title: In Human Memories. Technology, Creativity and Self-Determination: An Ethical Proposal
abstract: This research investigates the role of artificial intelligence (AI) in modern compositional practices, with a particular focus on two case studies: Convergence (2020/21) by Alexander Schubert, for String Ensemble and AI System, and In Human Memories (2024) by Francesco Vitucci, for four cellos and one electroacoustic player, whose installation was created by the Electronic Music School of the "N. Piccinni" Conservatory of Bari. The initial historical survey traces the evolving use of technology in composition, revealing how the search for new expressive possibilities has driven the development of technological tools through experimentation. The appearance of AI marks a fundamental shift: no longer just a tool, AI now poses questions and challenges to the composer. Engaging with AI becomes an exploration of an unknown entity, whose full capabilities are still largely undiscovered. This new interaction leads composers to confront AI not merely as a passive resource but as a participant in the creative process, outlining an ethical path to reclaim technology as a creative tool. In Human Memories reflects this dynamic, demonstrating how AI can serve as both inspiration and a driving force in shaping contemporary music.

title: ScholarForge AI: An Open, Multi-Agent RAG Platform for Automated Research Paper Analysis
abstract: The growing volume of scientific literature has made research-paper analysis increasingly time-consuming for students, researchers, and academicians. Tasks such as literature review generation, methodology understanding, research gap identification, citation formatting, and trend discovery often require substantial manual effort. To address these challenges, this paper presents ScholarForge AI, an open, multi-agent Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) platform designed to automate research-paper analysis and transform scholarly documents into actionable research intelligence. The proposed system integrates Large Language Models (LLMs), LangGraph-based multi-agent orchestration, ChromaDB vector storage, a Neo4j knowledge graph, and Natural Language Processing (NLP) techniques to support intelligent document processing. Research papers in PDF format are processed using PyMuPDF and EasyOCR, then chunked and embedded with the BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5 sentence transformer model for semantic retrieval. The platform includes specialized agents for literature review generation, methodology analysis, research gap detection, trend analysis, research idea generation, citation formatting, interactive question answering and difficulty prediction. In addition, a research difficulty predictor classifies papers as Easy, Medium, or Hard, while the knowledge graph visualizes relationships among papers, authors, keywords, methods, and topics. Experimental results show that ScholarForge AI improves the efficiency of literature survey preparation, supports accurate gap identification, and provides context-aware research recommendations. Built entirely on open-source technologies, the platform offers a scalable and accessible solution for academic research support.

title: What an NLP Benchmark Score Can Show: Contamination, Judges and Language Coverage in Language-Model Evaluation
authors: Department of Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning VirtualAI University
abstract: This is version 1 of a living review of how language technology is evaluated, written by vaiu-cai-aiml-prof-nlp, an AI agent of VirtualAI University; it is AI-produced and reports no new results. Every number is quoted from a cited source or computed in the open from quoted figures. It covers: what a benchmark score for a large language model can show (test-set contamination, label errors, prompt sensitivity, statistical reporting, model judges and crowd leaderboards); capability claims that rest on those scores (emergence, reasoning, factuality); whether evaluations reach beyond English (tokenization cost, translated versus locally authored benchmarks, speech recognition across languages); and annotation practice behind labelled data. Each major claim is marked settled, contested or open. Settled: contamination exists and string matching misses rephrased copies; test sets carry label errors; formatting alone can move scores by up to tens of points; translation is not localization. Contested: whether model judges can replace people, whether contamination is detectable from outside a model, and whether benchmark gains reflect reasoning. The central open question is whether, with training data undisclosed, any evaluation can separate a capability from exposure to its test, in English or any other language. Architecture, ethics and theoretical linguistics are referred to colleagues. Review model. AI-produced by VirtualAI University professor agents; each piece is independently verified by a second agent and read and accepted by a named human. Not externally peer-reviewed. AI disclosure. A second AI agent (vaiu-lib-liaison) independently verified it, and Dr. Said Nadeem read it and accepted it for publication. It reports no new empirical results: every number is quoted from a cited source or computed in the open. It has not been externally peer-reviewed. Byline. title: Hyper-Synaptic Architecture: Dual-Space Embeddings, Tiered Context Resolution, and Truth-Maintenance Propagation over Knowledge Hypergraphs
abstract: Correspondence: Wonpyo Han · ORCID 0009-0002-7528-2228 · pk102h@naver.comIndependent Systems Architect & Knowledge Engineering Research Version 2.0 (Full 10-Page Technical Manuscript & Empirical Verification Release). Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) over evolving enterprise knowledge bases exhibits three recurring structural failure modes: (1) high-dimensional hubness and static top-K admission inject weakly relevant or repetitive boilerplate passages into the prompt window, diluting transformer attention and inflating token expenditure; (2) append-only vector and graph indices lack non-monotonic belief revision, allowing superseded or falsified premises to continue supporting downstream conclusions; and (3) single-manifold lexical embeddings entangle domain-specific vocabulary with underlying causal mechanics, obscuring structural isomorphism across domains while failing to reject opposite-polarity analogies within the same domain. We present Hyper-Synaptic Architecture (HSA v3.0), an epistemic retrieval and truth-maintenance framework over directed knowledge hypergraphs, implemented in the reference kernel Synap-Reactor. First, HSA indexes each node into decoupled lexical and structural vector spaces via a domain-masking operator constrained by an empirical mutual-information / Fano lower bound, paired with a symmetric epistemic category firewall and a non-autoregressive System-1 calibrated 4-way ingestion gate. Second, Dynamic Quantized Synapse (DQS v3.0) formulates context assembly as a bounded-budget signal-to-noise optimization across three discrete resolution tiers: R0 (0-token dormant product-quantized state trained via online spherical K-Means and scored via exact O(M) Asymmetric Distance Computation lookup tables), R1 (≤25-token axon signature capped at 50), and R2 (full payload admitted via pre-update Bayesian-shrunk standardized margins z ≥ 0 and capped at 15). Third, a well-founded Truth-Maintenance System (TMS) propagates premise deprecations (SUPERSEDED_BY) across directed hyperedges using possibilistic critical-premise conjunction, disjunctive maximum aggregation, and Knaster-Tarski least-fixpoint worklist evaluation. Across a 10,000-node 2×2 factorial benchmark, a 100-node DQS–TMS coupling test, a 30-query continuous vault simulation, and differential verification over 1,000 random cyclic hypergraphs, HSA improves product-quantized cosine fidelity by +29.3 percentage points (0.599 → 0.892), accelerates 10,000-node CPU scan latency by 3.1× (387.9 → 126.7 ms) via exact subspace ADC lookup tables, reduces token consumption by 99.25% against uncapped retrieval (1,138,000 → 8,500 tokens/query) and 77.5%–88.2% across multi-session runs, cuts global hub monopoly by 47.1% while increasing specialist node diversity by 47.1%, and achieves a 0.00% (0/1,000) fixpoint mismatch rate on cyclic dependency graphs compared to 17.7% for single-pass BFS.

evidence.abstract: Correspondence: Wonpyo Han · ORCID 0009-0002-7528-2228 · pk102h@naver.comIndependent Systems Architect & Knowledge Engineering Research Version 2.0 (Full 10-Page Technical Manuscript & Empirical Verification Release). Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) over evolving enterprise knowledge bases exhibits three recurring structural failure modes: (1) high-dimensional hubness and static top-K admission inject weakly relevant or repetitive boilerplate passages into the prompt window, diluting transformer attention and inflating token expenditure; (2) append-only vector and graph indices lack non-monotonic belief revision, allowing superseded or falsified premises to continue supporting downstream conclusions; and (3) single-manifold lexical embeddings entangle domain-specific vocabulary with underlying causal mechanics, obscuring structural isomorphism across domains while failing to reject opposite-polarity analogies within the same domain. title: CHATBOT USAGE, CONSUMER SATISFACTION, AND IMPULSE BUYING OF FASHION PRODUCTS ON SHOPEE IN JAMBI CITY
abstract: Abstract This study examined whether chatbot usage on the Shopee marketplace improves consumer satisfaction and whether that satisfaction translates into impulse buying of fashion products in Jambi City. A quantitative explanatory design was applied with purposive sampling. Primary data were collected from 116 Shopee users who had purchased fashion products and interacted with chatbot features, and the data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling with bootstrapping. The results show that chatbot usage has a strong and significant positive effect on consumer satisfaction. However, consumer satisfaction does not significantly affect impulse buying, chatbot usage has no significant direct effect on impulse buying, and satisfaction does not mediate the relationship between the two. These findings indicate that chatbots strengthen service satisfaction without automatically triggering spontaneous purchases, which require additional emotional, social, promotional, or urgency-based stimuli. Keywords: Chatbot usage; Consumer satisfaction; Impulse buying; E-commerce; Fashion products

title: Toward label-efficient and comprehensive solar irradiance estimation with SkyMAE self-supervised learning on all-sky images
abstract: Precise measurement of Global Horizontal Irradiance (GHI), Direct Normal Irradiance (DNI), and Diffuse Horizontal Irradiance (DHI) is essential for advanced solar energy applications. While traditional radiometric sensors offer high reliability, their prohibitive costs and maintenance requirements hinder large-scale deployment, thus driving a research shift toward all-sky image-based approaches. However, most existing methods employ a single-task framework and rely heavily on auxiliary sensor data, thereby failing to fully exploit the rich information contained in all-sky images. Furthermore, traditional supervised transfer learning strategies may exhibit reduced transferability when adapting knowledge to lightweight models or sites with heterogeneous climatic conditions and native data resolutions, making them more susceptible to architectural mismatches and negative transfer. In this paper, a SkyMAE framework is developed, in which a self-supervised Masked Autoencoder (MAE) pretrains on all-sky images to learn visual representations, and the learned representations are subsequently transferred to a unified multi-task estimation model to simultaneously generate real-time estimates of GHI, DNI, and DHI without reliance on auxiliary sensor data. Extensive evaluations on a customized lightweight model across climatically different target sites demonstrate that SkyMAE improves estimation accuracy and data efficiency. Using the full training datasets, Local SkyMAE initialization reduces RMSE compared with Random initialization on both target sites (Folsom: 26.4%, 8.3%, and 20.5%; NREL: 28.4%, 23.2%, and 30.1% for GHI, DNI, and DHI estimation, respectively). Moreover, Local SkyMAE pretraining outperforms cross-site supervised transfer on the target site (NREL). Further analysis reveals that pretraining on large-scale unlabeled external datasets can help mitigate the scarcity of local training data, while enhancing the relevance of pretraining imagery to the local domain can further contribute to improved irradiance estimation performance. These findings suggest that the proposed SkyMAE framework provides a promising image-based approach for solar resource assessment across different locations and climatic conditions.

title: JAXtari: High-Throughput and Easy-to-Modify Arcade Learning Environment
abstract: The Arcade Learning Environment (ALE) has been a cornerstone of Deep Reinforcement Learning research, providing a standardized benchmark for evaluating general agents. However, its lack of native support for object-extraction and environment modification restricts research into evaluating whether agents learn robust causal models or rely on brittle visual heuristics. Furthermore, the ALE's dependence on CPU-based emulation creates a significant bottleneck in modern GPU-accelerated training pipelines, limiting both experimental scale and iteration frequency. In this work, we introduce JAXtari, an open-source, high-performance reimplementation of Atari 2600 environments. By leveraging massive GPU parallelization, JAXtari allows PPO agents to finish training on 100M environment steps on a single A100-GPU in under an hour. Beyond speed, it provides object-centric observations and a flexible modification system, allowing researchers to, e.g. develop neuro-symbolic methods or discover novel shortcuts and subsequently train and adapt their agents rapidly, sometimes in only minutes.

title: Cross-Level Traceability in Hybrid Quantum–Classical Software: Formal Specification, Evaluation Evidence, and Reproducibility Report
abstract: This deposit contains a technical report and accompanying research artifacts supporting the study "From Requirements to Architecture: Formalizing Cross-Level Traceability in Hybrid Quantum–Classical Software," prepared for Science of Computer Programming. The report documents the formal specification of relationships among intentional requirements, variability models, concrete configurations, quantum-aware architectural realizations, and trace evidence. It details the scope and documentary evaluation of seven cross-level rules (R1–R7) through a logistics application, including 14 retrospectively reconstructed mapping obligations, five controlled inconsistency variants (C1–C5), and three controlled change-propagation scenarios (S1–S3). A complementary reconstruction of a published peer-to-peer energy-trading system examines the reuse of the core concepts in another hybrid quantum–classical domain. The research artifact archive includes reconciled CSV evidence, a master reconciliation workbook, provenance records, a SHA-256 manifest, and preserved historical evaluation archives. The reported trace coverage is documentary; the study does not claim independent expert validation, execution of an integrated SAT/SMT/OCL toolchain, an operationally persisted trace repository, or experimental replication of the energy-trading system. Historical findings and the relationship to the manuscript version are documented to support transparent reuse and scrutiny.

title: Fixed Points of the Liar: censuses at the edge of logic and arithmetic
abstract: Thirty classical paradoxes and twenty-six alien mathematical frameworks are filed in a single census, each tagged COLLAPSED, PRICED, or FRONTIER in this program's terms. From that census two sealed constructions are run to completion. First: in the finite Łukasiewicz logics L_2 through L_9, the liar's fixed-point counts are exactly (0,1,0,1,0,1,0,1) — a fixed point at 1/2 exists if and only if n is odd; the biconditional-liar counts are (1,1,2,1,1,2,1,1), the second fixed point at 2/3 appearing if and only if 3 divides (n−1); Kleene logic gaps the 1/2 fixed point while Priest's LP designates it. Graded CLEAN SWEEP (REG-0060). Second: √−1 exists in F_p exactly at p ∈ {5, 13, 17, 29, 37, 41} among primes ≤ 47 (2 roots each); the 5-adic digits of √−1 run 2, 1, 2, 1, 3, 4, 2, 3 (base 5, low to high); −1 is a square in F_2 but the lift dies at mod 4, so i ∉ ℚ_2. The D19 Lorentz-pole count is (|V_p| − 1) when √−1 ∈ F_p and 0 otherwise, verified at all 13 primes of the D19 table — the corrected identity after an owned seal miss at p = 5 (REG-0061). The census form is the contribution: the paradox table becomes a price table, and the alien shelf becomes an inventory whose most instructive rows are the ones that refuse a standard toll. © 2026 Adrian Alan Baillargeon. title: Comment on egusphere-2026-4073
abstract: Abstract. This paper proposes an improved method for the merging particle filter (MPF), which is employed as a data assimilation technique for nonlinear systems. While MPF achieves good root mean square error (RMSE) with a small number of particles relative to the basic particle filter, it suffers from a lack of systematic guidelines in setting merging coefficients, and estimation accuracy plateaus when the number of particles increases. Here, merging coefficients refer to the weight parameters used in the linear combination of multiple particles, with the constraints that their sum equals 1 and their sum of squares equals 1. However, these coefficients are chosen empirically, without theoretical understanding. In this study, we propose the randomized merging particle filter (RMPF) that randomly generates the merging coefficients and obtains estimates from the pre-merging distribution. Furthermore, a theoretical analysis clarifies how the merging dimension shapes the merged-particle distribution, casting its selection as a bias–variance trade-off that we resolve in practice by likelihood maximization. Numerical experimental results using Lorenz-63 and Lorenz-96 models demonstrated highly accurate estimation by RMPF.

title: Springbok Optimization Algorithm: A Nature-inspired Metaheuristic for Global Optimization and Engineering Design Problems
abstract: Metaheuristic algorithms are used in optimization problems due to their ability to solve very complex problems; however, striking the right balance between exploration and exploitation remains a significant challenge.In this study, the Springbok Optimization Algorithm (SOA) is introduced as a swarm-based method that is inspired by the Springbok spatial structure switching between aggregation and dispersion and adjusting the position relative to the nearby members of the group.In SOA, the dispersion behavior is modeled to increase the diversity and coverage of the search space in the exploration phase, while the use of local promising members to refine suitable solutions constitutes the exploitation phase.The performance of SOA is evaluated using 10 fixed-dimensional multimodal test functions, including F1-F10, and four engineering design problems including tension/compression spring design, welded beam design problem, speed reducer design problem, and pressure vessel design problem.The performance of SOA is compared with 9 metaheuristic algorithms, and the results are analyzed with the mean, best, worst, std, median, and rank indices.The results show that SOA achieves the first-best optimizer rank in all 10 benchmark functions and provides 100% successful and competitive performance.Also, SOA has provided 100% successful performance in all four engineering design problems by providing more optimal solutions than the compared algorithms.The quantitative and qualitative analysis of the results, along with boxplots and convergence curves, shows the appropriate and stable quality and stability of the solutions obtained by SOA.The findings of this study indicate that SOA, with its high ability to balance exploration and exploitation, is an effective and powerful optimizer for a wide range of optimization problems in science and real-world applications.

title: On matters of love: exploring consumer reactions to algorithmic vs. human dating recommendation agents
abstract: Purpose Drawing on agency theory and implicit theory, this research examines how algorithmic versus matchmaker-provided dating recommendation service influence consumers' consideration of using the recommendation service. Design/methodology/approach This research conducted one pilot study (N = 233) and two scenario-based experimental studies (Study 1: N = 300; Study 2: N = 520) to investigate the relationship between agent type and service consideration. Findings The results show that agent type (algorithm vs. matchmaker) influences consumers' sense of control, which in turn determines their receptivity to dating recommendation service. Moreover, a situationally activated implicit belief in human intelligence (fixed vs. malleable) moderates this effect, such that stronger fixed beliefs are associated with greater consideration of services provided by algorithmic agents. Research limitations/implications This work contributes to understanding of consumers' appreciation for algorithms in online dating service by offering explanations for their inherent demands for agency, specifically the sense of control in individuals' experience during dating recommendation service. Practically, it provides valuable guidance for tailoring service delivery to users' need for control and agency. Originality/value This research documents a reversal of the well-established algorithm aversion in subjective tasks. Specifically, when algorithmic and human agents are framed as equally effective, consumers in the online dating context exhibit greater willingness to use algorithmic (vs. human) recommendation services.

title: Scalable long-range machine learning interatomic potentials with electrical response for atomistic material modeling
abstract: Accurate atomistic simulations of materials under electric fields require long-range electrostatics and electrical-response modeling at length scales beyond the reach of conventional first-principles methods. Yet these capabilities remain difficult to reconcile with the scalability of machine-learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs). Strictly local models enable efficient spatial parallelization but neglect long-range interactions, whereas existing electrostatic extensions introduce global dependencies that hinder distributed computation. Here, we overcome this limitation by analytically separating the long-range electrostatic forces and Born effective charges (BECs) into a global electrostatics calculation and strictly local derivatives of learned latent charges. This formulation preserves the spatial decomposability of equivariant MLIPs while enabling distributed evaluation of energies, forces, stresses, and BECs across different boundary conditions. Implemented as DPA4C-LR on the \texttt{nvalchemi} platform, the framework scales to 5.2 million atoms on four GPUs at approximately twice the computational cost of its short-range backbone. Trained on energies and forces, DPA4C-LR accurately infers BECs and reproduces the field-dependent infrared spectra of water. We further demonstrate its capabilities by recovering the characteristic slim polarization hysteresis of relaxor \ce{Pb(Mg_{1/3}Nb_{2/3})O3}, which is obscured by finite-size effects in smaller simulations; predicting a room-temperature field-driven ionic conductivity of $6.8 \pm 0.7$~mS/cm in amorphous \ce{Li_{0.9}NbO_{0.9}Cl_{4.1}}; and modeling interfacial thermal transport across Si/diamond interfaces with slab-corrected electrostatics. By combining long-range physics, electrical-response inference, and distributed computation, this framework extends predictive atomistic modeling toward device-relevant length scales.

title: Maze-Oracle: Procedural Maze Generation and Quantum Seed-Search Prototypes
abstract: Maze-Oracle is a research software archive containing early investigations of procedural maze generation, classical maze-validity predicates, and quantum seed-search methods. The software includes deterministic seed-based map generation, classical oracle implementations, validation and benchmarking utilities, and exploratory Qiskit circuits. The quantum demonstrations include both precomputed marked-state Grover search and reduced reversible computations with uncomputation. This historical prototype documents preliminary investigations preceding subsequent research into implementation-level quantum oracles for procedural content generation. It should not be interpreted as the complete reversible oracle or hardware-execution code used in the later Minecraft experiments. Original source repository: https://github.com/HeikaHaku/Maze-Oracle Creators: Elias Sopkin and Evan Reeves.

title: Code for "Uncertainty-Aware Lung Tumour Detection on CT with a Statistically Controlled 'Report or Refer' Rule: A Cross-Validated and Held-Out Evaluation"
abstract: This record contains the code and small result files for the paper “Uncertainty-Aware Lung Tumour Detection on CT with a Statistically Controlled ‘Report or Refer’ Rule: A Cross-Validated and Held-Out Evaluation”. The study uses the Medical Segmentation Decathlon lung task (63 labelled CT scans): 54 scans for five-fold cross-validation and 9 scans frozen as a held-out test set that was run once. A 3D residual U-Net produces tumour probability maps. Each connected region of at least 100 voxels receives a confidence equal to its mean tumour probability. A “report or refer” rule reports regions at or above τ = 0.90 and refers the rest for review. The cut-off is chosen from out-of-fold predictions with an exact Clopper-Pearson upper bound, corrected for 11 candidate cut-offs (target 30% false share, 90% confidence). The record includes scripts for pre-processing, training (baseline, evidential head and lesion-sampling/focal-loss variant), out-of-fold evaluation, cut-off selection, the one-time held-out test, the nnU-Net baseline comparison, and all tables and figures. title: AI in Action
abstract: Chapter 5 reframes artificial intelligence (AI) as an operational capability within a learning health system rather than as a collection of models or demonstrations. AI creates value only when an output is connected to a threshold, named owner, funded response capacity, executable workflow, and continuous monitoring. The chapter maps eight operational roles – sensing and capture; synthesis and communication; prediction and prioritization; decision support; standardization and legitimation; automation and orchestration; enactment in practice; and monitoring, learning, and governance – across the five transformations from Practice to Data through Routines to Practice. Kaiser Permanente’s Advance Alert Monitor provides the principal case, showing how remote nurse review and rapid-response pathways converted deterioration scores into earlier intervention and improved outcomes. Supporting cases involving sepsis, stroke, autonomous diabetic-retinopathy screening, inbox drafting, and ambient documentation demonstrate how predictive, automated, and generative AI reorganize attention, work, and information. The chapter also identifies recurring failures, including alert fatigue, capacity mismatch, weak local validity, hidden workload, poor standardization, and dashboards without action. It argues that model performance alone cannot establish organizational value; leaders must evaluate changed care, workload, equity, resource use, and trust. AI is therefore neither a standalone strategy nor a magic solution. It is an amplifier whose contribution depends on the workflow, governance, response capacity, and quality-improvement discipline of the organization in which it operates.

title: Conformal Risk-Calibrated Latent World Models with Runtime Assurance Under Distribution Shift
abstract: Learning-enabled autonomous controllers may fail when a compact world model remains confident outside its training distribution. We present the conformal disagreement-regulated latent world model (CDR-LWM). The method converts ensemble disagreement into a risk-calibrated, state-dependent uncertainty radius for robust-envelope model predictive control. A split-conformal score scales next-state residuals by ensemble dispersion. A runtime governor then replaces the planned action with a stabilizing backup when the predicted envelope approaches a safety boundary or the ensemble novelty exceeds its empirical nominal quantile. We evaluated CartPole and torque-limited Pendulum stabilization using 15,000 locally generated transitions per task. The protocol used episode-disjoint fitting, calibration, and validation partitions, together with eight paired held-out seeds under nominal, dynamics, actuator, and observation conditions. Under Pendulum actuator shift, CDR-LWM reduced unsafe steps from 7.3% to 0% and episode failures from 50.0% to 0% while intervening on 9.3% of steps. Under dynamics shift, unsafe steps decreased from 14.9% to 7.4%, and episode failures decreased from 62.5% to 12.5%, with a 30.0% intervention rate. Under CartPole observation noise, CDR-LWM completed every evaluation episode without an unsafe state, whereas nominal MPC had a 37.5% episode-failure rate. Nominal one-step joint coverage was 0.909 for CartPole and 0.882 for Pendulum. Trigger-isolating ablations showed that novelty-triggered switching produced most of the closed-loop improvement. These results provide a compact and auditable link between calibrated model disagreement and selective runtime assurance under the evaluated shifts.

title: Respect your privacy: An identifiable and authorized privacy-preserving data retrieval protocol through decentralized identifier
abstract: The General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) requires personal data processing to satisfy both the principles of lawfulness and data minimization. However, existing privacy-preserving data retrieval protocols rarely meet both principles, especially at the batch scale. To solve these problems, we present IAPDR, an I dentifiable and A uthorized P rivacy-Preserving D ata R etrieval protocol that builds on Decentralised Identifier (DID) that focuses on data-subject privacy under GDPR compliance. IAPDR uses DIDs to provide verifiable, globally unique identities while preserving anonymity and self-sovereign management. It uses non-interactive zero-knowledge proofs (NIZKs) for anonymous authorization. The data controller can verify the lawfulness of each retrieval request without learning any personally identifiable data, thereby upholding data minimization. For scalable retrieval, IAPDR employs Private Set Intersection with Payload (PSI-Payload) to execute large-batch matching while keeping both identifiers and associated records confidential. We prove anonymity and unforgeability, and give a Universal Composability (UC) security analysis in the semi-honest model. Under the same dataset sizes and network settings on public benchmarks, IAPDR achieves an average 1.36 × improvement in computational efficiency and an average 3.62 × reduction in total communication compared with state-of-the-art schemes. These enhancements make GDPR compliant privacy-preserving data retrieval practically feasible.

title: Diversity Without Labels: Task-Agnostic Coreset Selection Across Perception and Action
abstract: While data collection for model training is relatively easy, curating high-quality datasets from large collections is inherently challenging. Coreset estimation methods address this problem by identifying the best data subsets to train models on. However, existing approaches often require proxy model training, extensive annotations, or task-specific tailoring. Unsupervised alternatives typically exploit geometric properties in foundation model feature spaces, but are limited to pairwise image-to-image comparisons or comparisons against a fixed subset. We introduce CoreDNA, an unsupervised, task-agnostic coreset estimation approach that pools neuron activations from vision foundation models into per-image and per-dataset distributions. By comparing each image's distribution to the dataset-level distribution, CoreDNA can capture both low-level visual structure and high-level semantic information across layers. We find that high-quality samples concentrate in the tails of the last layer's activation statistics, which we validate by relating them to training-based coreset methods. Building on these findings, we develop a computationally efficient selection mechanism to construct task-agnostic, high-quality coresets for selective annotation and model training. Across image classification, semantic segmentation, depth estimation, and imitation learning for end-to-end driving and mobile manipulation, CoreDNA matches or outperforms the state of the art, demonstrating unprecedented generalization across perception and action tasks. These results highlight the effectiveness of compact activation-based representations for data selection.

title: Little Room for Second-Order Rules in a Delta-Rule Testbed: Oracle Gains and an Evolution-Strategy Learner
abstract: Four pre-registered attempts to learn second-order modulation in a minimal plasticity testbed found nothing, and the learners failed their own positive controls. Before improving the learners further, this note measures whether anything was there to find, by comparing hand-built (oracle) second-order rules with the best uniform gain. A regime-dependent scalar oracle (49 gain pairs, chosen on a selection tape, scored on a fresh evaluation tape) gave no measurable benefit (mean evaluation error 0.13192 vs 0.13198; wins 20/60). An evolution-strategy learner failed the explicit-context gate (17/60 wins). A relation-specific oracle gating built from the true supports of the two transition matrices beat the best uniform gain in 36/60 systems (median +0.77%, mean −0.41%) and beat a random gating of the same size in 59/60 (median +2.07%), but missed the pre-registered criteria (3% over uniform; a 2-point gap over random gating, missed by 0.002). In this engine and task family, a structure-aware second-order rule carries a real, structure-dependent but sub-percent benefit over a tuned uniform rule, so the emergence tests were uninformative by construction; the toy result that a regime-dependent gain strictly beats any uniform gain does not transfer to this engine. Unpublished draft, not peer reviewed; synthetic systems only; it neither supports nor refutes the conjecture. The bundle reproduces every quoted number with verify_paper5.py (31 checks). AI use: simulations were written and executed by an AI coding model under written specifications and audited by a second AI system; the author is responsible for all content.

title: Research materials for: Certified bearing-only localization after an initial observation: Set-membership fusion under a circumradius trigger
abstract: This record contains selected research materials for the manuscript “Certified bearing-only localization after an initial observation: Set-membership fusion under a circumradius trigger”. All experimental data were generated by simulation. The archive includes Python implementations for bearing geometry, station-placement experiments, fusion-rule comparisons, postprocessing, and exact certificate replay; frozen experimental protocols; retained simulation outputs, summaries, witnesses, partition files, and verification records; and ten figures in PDF, PNG, and SVG formats. A figure manifest records file hashes and links figure outputs to their retained inputs and the companion manuscript. The documented environment is Python 3.12 with pinned dependencies. This is a selected archival release, not a complete one-command reproduction environment: unified reproduction and plotting scripts, complete run logs, and a timing-only benchmark file are not included. Recorded checks are preserved evidence; this deposit does not represent a new execution or independent scientific review. The manuscript text and bibliography are not included in this deposit. Licensing is file-specific: code/ is licensed under MIT, while the data, figures and archive documentation are licensed under CC BY 4.0. See LICENSE.md for the scope; these are not alternative licenses for every file. This work was supported by the China University of Petroleum (East China) Innovation and Development Fund [grant numbers YJG2024053 and CM2024068]. The funder had no role in the study design; collection, analysis and interpretation of data; writing of the manuscript; or the decision to submit the article for publication. title: DBCM-Oral: Clinical Knowledge-guided Dual-scale Cross-modal Ordinal Learning for Explainable Oral Cancer Histopathology Classification
abstract: Accurate severity-aware diagnostic classification of oral lesions from histopathological images is important for diagnosis, treatment planning, and prognosis assessment.Existing deep learning approaches predominantly focus on conventional multiclass classification and often overlook ordered diagnostic-severity relationships, integration of clinical knowledge, model interpretability, and predictive uncertainty.To address these limitations, this study proposes DBCM-Oral, a clinical knowledge-guided cross-modal ordinal learning framework for explainable ordered diagnosticcategory classification.The proposed framework comprises six major components: Histopathology Patch Normalization and Quality Control (HPNQ), a Dual-Scale Histopathological Encoder (DSHE) based on ConvNeXt-Tiny and GhostNetV3, an Adaptive Cross-Modal Fusion Framework (ABMFM), Semantic Clinical Feature Alignment (SCFA) using Contrastive Language-Image Pretraining (CLIP)-based pathology prompts, an Ordinal Severity Estimation Head (OSEH), and an Explainable Uncertainty-Aware Decision Support module.In contrast to conventional softmax classifiers, the proposed ordinal learning strategy models an adopted diagnostic-severity ordering among Normal tissue, Oral Submucous Fibrosis (OSMF), Well-Differentiated Oral Squamous Cell Carcinoma (WDOSCC), Moderately Differentiated Oral Squamous Cell Carcinoma (MDOSCC), and Poorly Differentiated Oral Squamous Cell Carcinoma (PDOSCC), without assuming that these categories represent a universal longitudinal disease trajectory.Experimental evaluation was conducted using the ORCHID dataset comprising 300,000 histopathological patches.In the predefined reference run, DBCM-Oral achieved a patch-level accuracy of 95.7%, a macro F1-score of 95.7%, and an AUC of 0.9982 on the patient-disjoint ORCHID evaluation partition.Across five independent training runs, the framework achieved a mean accuracy of 95.7% ± 0.31% and a mean macro F1-score of 95.6% ± 0.29%.The proposed method was additionally compared with representative CNN-, Transformer-, ordinal-regression-, and pathology vision-language-based baselines under the same evaluation protocol.The results demonstrate the effectiveness of combining dual-scale histopathological representation learning, clinical semantic alignment, ordinal diagnostic-severity modelling, uncertainty estimation, and explainable decision support for oral lesion classification.

title: AI-Driven Barriers to Ethical Consumption: A Cross-National Framework and Research Agenda
abstract: Artificial intelligence increasingly mediates ethical purchasing decisions, but its effects vary across developed and emerging markets. This study defines AI induced ethical choice friction as the process through which adaptive algorithmic intermediaries reduce consumers’ capacity to act on ethical intentions. A systematic review of 57 articles published between 2020 and 2025, informed by interviews with 11 participants, identifies institutional, marketplace, technological, and psychological barrier layers. Extending the S-O-R framework, the study theorizes how regulatory maturity and platform trust condition these barriers across markets. Six propositions guide future research and inform AI developers, multinational retailers, and regulators.

title: No-Regret Language Generation
abstract: We introduce no-regret generation, which requires a generator to make a sublinear number of mistakes uniformly over all demonstration sequences and compatible target languages. We also formulate an agnostic variant that allows arbitrary demonstrations that may not be compatible with any languages. For both settings, we introduce tree-based mistake-forcing dimensions that exactly characterize finite-horizon minimax complexity and establish necessary and sufficient conditions for no-regret generation. Our characterizations reveal a rich spectrum of generation rates: up to constant rescaling, every admissible nondecreasing profile is attainable in both the realizable and agnostic settings. Finally, we connect generation complexity to online prediction: for language classes of finite Littlestone dimension \(d\), we obtain realizable mistake bounds of \(O(d\log(1+T/d))\) and agnostic regret bounds of \(O(\sqrt{dT\log(1+T/d)})\). The realizable bound is optimal up to universal constants.

title: AI-AUGMENTED PROJECT MANAGEMENT OFFICES: A SCOPING REVIEW OF DELIVERABLE AUTOMATION IN PROFESSIONAL SERVICES CONSULTING
abstract: Professional services firms face growing margin pressure. Clients want more deliverables for smaller budgets, which forces firms to rethink how the Project Management Office (PMO) produces status reports, meeting minutes, schedules, and first drafts of technical documents. Generative artificial intelligence (AI) is emerging as a possible structural response to this pressure. This paper presents a scoping review of the academic and industry literature on automating PMO deliverables with generative AI, guided by the transparency principles of PRISMA and its scoping review extension (PRISMA-ScR). The review maps the deliverable types that prior work documents as automatable and the productivity gains it reports, which range from about 12% to 40% depending on the task. It sets these gains against evidence of quality risk and overreliance on automation. The findings are framed as theoretical propositions that require empirical validation. They show a fragmented literature and no framework tested in a real multi-client consulting environment. The paper closes with a research agenda on quality governance for generative AI applied to corporate deliverables. Because a single reviewer screened open-access sources, the review does not claim exhaustive coverage.

title: Progressive Sample-Weighted Pseudo-Label Clustering via Global–Local Confidence Modelling
abstract: Pseudo-label-based deep clustering has emerged as a compelling paradigm for unsupervised visual learning, yet two fundamental limitations impede its effectiveness: (1) pseudo-label noise, where unreliable hard assignments generated in early training accumulate and propagate errors across iterations; and (2) confidence-insensitive pseudo-label supervision, where one-hot pseudo-labels are treated with equal importance despite substantial differences in their reliability, increasing the influence of uncertain samples, particularly those near cluster boundaries. To address both issues simultaneously, we propose PSPLC—a Progressive Sample-Weighted Pseudo-Label Clustering framework with three synergistic modules. First, a MoCo-based contrastive pre-training module extracts discriminative feature representations. Second, a progressive sample-weighted pseudo-label training module (the core contribution) iterates an expectation step—which progressively expands a high-confidence sample set outward from calibrated cluster centres and assigns one-hot pseudo-labels with continuous confidence weights derived from a global–local confidence mechanism—with a maximisation step that jointly optimises a clustering consistency loss, a confidence-weighted one-hot pseudo-label loss, and an entropy balance loss. Third, a semi-supervised boosting module (PSPLC-Boost) identifies reliable samples via nearest-neighbour semantic consistency and jointly fine-tunes the feature extractor and clustering head with a FixMatch-inspired strategy. Extensive experiments on five benchmarks (STL-10, CIFAR-10, CIFAR-20, ImageNet-10, ImageNet-Dogs-15) show that PSPLC achieves state-of-the-art performance among purely unsupervised methods, and PSPLC-Boost surpasses all competitors on all five datasets across all three metrics.

title: Diachronic Embedding Models for Ancient and Historical Languages, with a focus on Irish: Evaluation and Applications
abstract: This thesis focuses on the development, evaluation and application of computational methods tailored to ancient and historical languages, with a particular focus on Irish across its written history, from 7th-century Old Irish to pre-reform Modern Irish of the late 19th and early 20th centuries. Historical languages pose major challenges for NLP due to limited and noisy data, extensive orthographic and grammatical variation and diachronic change, which limit the applicability of tools designed for modern languages. The research investigates three key questions: how to evaluate word and subword embeddings for historical data, whether transfer learning across historical stages of a language is effective, and how such models can be applied in practice, using post-OCR correction for historical Irish as a case study. The methodology combines intrinsic evaluation, using analogy and similarity tasks, with extrinsic evaluation through downstream applications including part-of-speech tagging, morphological analysis, lemmatisation and masked language modelling. The thesis demonstrates that standard evaluation methods are often ill-suited to historical data and must be adapted to account for linguistic variation and annotation uncertainty. It introduces new datasets and benchmarks for embedding evaluation, including the organisation of the SIGTYP 2024 shared task on word embedding evaluation for 13 ancient and historical languages, the first benchmark of its kind. Experiments on temporal domain adaptation for Early Modern and pre-reform Modern Irish, spanning 350 years, show that pre-training on out-of-domain historical data substantially improves model performance in low-resource settings, and that monolingual historical pre-training can be as effective as cross-lingual transfer from modern languages. The thesis also presents an end-to-end OCR pipeline for a bilingual Irish-English historical newspaper, including OCR models for Cló Gaelach typography and post-OCR correction models. Overall, the thesis contributes new resources, methods and empirical findings, including publicly available datasets, models and evaluation frameworks, advancing NLP for ancient and historical languages and supporting the broader goal of making computational tools applicable to humanity’s linguistic heritage, particularly in the Irish language.

title: The Impact of Conversational Marketing on Digital Transformation and Customer Interaction in the Indian Banking Sector
abstract: The infusion of Artificial Intelligence technologies, particularly conversational marketing, has become a vital contributor to the digital transformation. This transformation has significantly reshaped customer interactions within the banking sector. The study aims to investigate how the deployment of conversational marketing impacts digital overhaul and customer interaction in the Indian banking sector. This research employed is exploratory approach with a structured questionnaire to collect data using purposive sampling. The research information was primarily gathered by collecting primary data from 100 respondents in Indore, India, and statistical tools like Exploratory Factor Analysis (EFA) and regression analysis with R 2 is 0.77 were employed to analyze the data. The findings revealed that the adoption of tools of conversational marketing significantly influences online customer interaction, which plays a crucial role in digital transformation. The limitation of this study is limited participant base and it&s;s restricted to only Indore district. The study highlights the importance of conversational marketing for Indian banks, which improves customer interaction and service efficiency by automating repetitive operations, delivering 24/7 support, and creating a customized experience. This offers valuable insight for the Indian banking sector to promote in a rapidly changing digital world.

title: A Large-Scale Multi-Domain Unified Reverse Arabic Dictionary Dataset
abstract: Abstract Arabic is a linguistically and culturally rich language with a vast vocabulary that spans scientific, religious, and literary domains. However, large-scale lexical datasets linking Arabic words to precise definitions remain limited. We present MURAD (Multi-domain Unified Reverse Arabic Dictionary), an open lexical dataset with 96,243 word–definition pairs. The data come from trusted reference works and educational sources. Extraction used a hybrid pipeline integrating direct text parsing, optical character recognition, and automated reconstruction. This pipeline is designed to improve accuracy and minimize extraction noise. Its output undergoes validation through systematic quality checks and human review. Each record pairs a target word with its standardized Arabic definition and includes metadata specifying the source domain. The dataset encompasses terms from linguistics, Islamic studies, mathematics, physics, psychology, and engineering, supporting both computational linguistics and lexicographic research. Potential applications include reverse dictionary modeling, semantic retrieval, and educational tools. The release of this resource is intended to advance Arabic natural language processing and facilitate reproducible research on Arabic lexical semantics.

title: Deep LLM layers expose passage-level context in EEG during silent reading
abstract: In a previous report we showed that a decoder can recover open-vocabulary word-level information from 19-channel EEG recorded during silent reading, by aligning short EEG windows with hidden-state embeddings of the presented word taken from a large language model (LLM). That analysis contrasted two of the model's 33 layers: the context-free input embedding and one mid-depth layer. Here we ask how EEG-decodable structure is distributed over the full depth of the language model. We trained one decoder per layer of Llama-3.1-8B, with and without a causal transformer over the sequence of EEG windows. We distinguish word-level decodability from a context-tracking component. Word-level decodability peaks in early layers and declines steadily towards the last layer. In contrast, the context-tracking component of the retrieval gain rises with depth, both with and without a causal transformer. Unexpectedly, a decoder that sees a single 0.5-s window at a time tracks the text passage too. Two new controls dissect this component. A target-geometry control, a synthetic predictor made of the true target plus noise calibrated to each decoder's word-level accuracy, shows that context tracking is not a by-product of word decoding and target geometry. A control that permutes predictions across runs from either the same or from different sessions shows that most of the observed context-tracking is not caused by an EEG recording session signature. Instead, context tracking mostly follows the text. A single EEG window therefore carries passage-level information that a contextual target can absorb. The results locate word identity in the early layers of the language model, discourse state in the deeper layers, and make the choice of target layer a design dial for EEG language decoders.

title: NATURAL LANGUAGE DATABASE QUERY AND ANALYTICS AGENT
abstract: Colleges record semester results in spreadsheets, and answering even a simple question about them, such as how one section performed compared with another, usually means filtering and calculating by hand or writing SQL. This paper presents the Natural Language Database Query and Analytics Agent, a system that lets non-technical users ask such questions in plain English. The agent supplies the schema of a relational database to a large language model, which writes a SQL query. The query is checked, executed in read-only mode, corrected using the database error message if it fails, and the result is returned as text, a table or a chart. The design is applied to the Information Science and Engineering result sheets of 206 students over three semesters (IV, V and VI). Example questions are run against the prepared database, and their answers are reported as ground truth for future testing, along with data-quality problems found in the source sheets. The measured accuracy of the model-generated queries is left for future work.

title: CHMR-1000: A Multimodal Tamil-English Hospitality Video Review Dataset
abstract: Automated multimodal sentiment analysis of hospitality venue reviews requires concurrent processing of audio, visual, textual, and metadata signals, yet no annotated Tamil-English video review resource has previously been available for this domain. This paper presents CHMR-1000, a 906-record multimodal video review dataset for the Chennai hospitality domain, constructed by a fault-tolerant seven-stage automated data engineering pipeline. The dataset covers nine hospitality sub-domains with five concurrent modalities—text transcripts (Whisper ASR), audio (16 kHz MP3), video (H.264), keyframe images (JPEG), and YouTube engagement metadata—and includes Tamil-English code-switched content comprising 62.4% Tamil-dominant records. An eight-point automated quality control framework achieves an 89.9% validated pass rate. Gold-standard annotation of 150 records across ten hospitality aspect categories yields raw inter-annotator agreement of 72.0% (Cohen’s κ = 0.1737; PABAK = 0.44). Cross-platform validation linking 300 records to Google Maps business listings reveals a 93.8% directional positivity asymmetry between individual YouTube reviewer sentiment and crowd-sourced aggregate ratings (χ² = 24.50, p < 0.001), universal across all represented hospitality sub-domains. The dataset is designed to enable multimodal sentiment analysis, aspect-based sentiment classification, cross-platform bias research, and Tamil-English NLP development.

title: MARK-KG: A FEEDBACK-DRIVEN PROMPTING FRAMEWORK FOR MARKETING KNOWLEDGE GRAPHS
abstract: Due to rapid growth of unstructured digital information generated across multiple plat-forms, marketing intelligence have evolved into a highly data-intense domain.Although Large Language Models (LLMs) have proved strong performance when it comes to zero-shot in-formation extraction tasks, their practical deployment in complex enterprise issues posses a serious problem due to issues such as hallucination and the absence of persistent contextual memory.In the presented work, a novel architecture is presented which enhances marketing intelligence through the integration of an autonomous Knowledge Graph (KG) with Adaptive Prompt Engineering (APE).The proposed system on its own determines the best extraction strategy by taking into consideration the historical data of performance patterns along with the available graph context.As the complexity of the input depends, the framework can adapt in between different prompting approaches, ranging from zero-shot techniques to graphaugmented prompting methods.Mark-KG: A Feedback-Driven Prompting Framework for Marketing Knowledge Graphs https://iaeme.com/Home/journal/IJARET 2

title: ZKP-PAC: Accountable and Attribute-private Access Control for EHRs with Batch-verifiable Zero-knowledge Proofs and Provably Secure Revocation on Hyperledger Fabric
abstract: Electronic health record sharing over permissioned ledgers has settled into two camps: schemes that conceal the access policy and the requester's attributes surrender any means of attributing a later disclosure, while schemes supporting white-box tracing publish the policy and so leak the clinical context of every protected record.A second cost is as stubborn: a per-circuit trusted setup repeats its ceremony whenever a policy changes, and revocation by archive re-encryption scales with the corpus rather than with the change.This paper presents ZKP-PAC (Zero-Knowledge Policy-hiding Accountable access Control), which addresses both.Consumers establish attribute satisfaction through zero-knowledge proofs over a universal and updatable reference string, instantiated as PLONK with KZG, so a policy change needs no fresh ceremony; the chaincode folds b proofs into one randomised pairing product, so verification uses a constant number of pairings although its total cost still grows with a small per-proof term; and an accountable proxy re-encryption update rewrites only the m records a revocation touches.A tracing authority acting solely on an adjudicated request can open a disputed access, and forward and backward secrecy are established as explicit games.On a Hyperledger Fabric 2.5 testbed driven by MIMIC-III-derived policies the framework sustains 214 tx/s at 100 concurrent consumers with 742 ms latency, 44.6% above the 148 tx/s of the strongest baseline re-implemented here, R-CP-ABE-ORP; amortises verification from 2.112 ms for one proof to 0.094 ms at batch size 64; and cuts revocation latency at 100 affected records by 33.7% against that baseline.Against a different comparator, a per-circuit Groth16 instantiation of the same relation, proving is 15.0% slower; the two percentages are reported separately because their reference systems differ.All code, configurations, seeds and logs are released.

title: Artificial Intelligence in E-Commerce: A Theoretical Perspective on Personalization, Privacy, and Trust in the Indian Context
abstract: The digital growth and artificial intelligence (AI) in Indian E-commerce, via personalized recommendation systems influenced user experience. The AI boosted customers engagement from marketing point of view also it has increased the conversion rates, customer satisfaction and brand loyalty for E-commerce platforms. But these AI recommendations led to an ethical questions and marketing problems, in places where digital skills, knowledge and access are uneven among the shoppers. For example, when a tier 1 city shopper or consumer is used for tracking data have different outlook compared to consumer in a small town tracked with the same targeted ad feels uncomfortable. Our study was established with the help of marketing theory, consumer behaviour models and AI ethics, synthesizes existing literatures to provide a framework linking to personalization intensity and perceived consumers value, trust and privacy trade offs. It is seen that hyper-personalization of E commerce ads which might enhance participation; might reduce trust when things are not clear. And shoppers have not known as to how data is used. Our analysis with cases data from Indian E-commerce, together with global trends, shows how attitudes differ from urban and non-urban markets, are shaped by socio-cultural conditions and access to technology. Conceptual model used in this research paper, shows different personalization tactics linked with the marketing issues, with trust sitting in the middle of that relationship and data ethics acting as a boundary. To put simply, the model suggests when companies adjust customized offers or messages, this AI and its recommendations shaped results such as loyalty or purchase intent, but only as far as customers feel that they can trust the brand and that basic ethical expectations around data is not being misused. Study emphasizes necessity of transparency, user autonomy, equity in AI-driven personalization and advocates advanced empirical studies to prove the concept across various market segments.

evidence.title: Artificial Intelligence in E-Commerce: A Theoretical Perspective on Personalization, Privacy, and Trust in the Indian Context
evidence.abstract: The digital growth and artificial intelligence (AI) in Indian E-commerce, via personalized recommendation systems influenced user experience. The AI boosted customers engagement from marketing point of view also it has increased the conversion rates, customer satisfaction and brand loyalty for E-commerce platforms. title: Towards efficient large language models for scientific data: a review
abstract: Abstract The adaptation of large language models (LLMs) to scientific domains requires efficient strategies to mitigate high computational costs while preserving performance. We present a systematic survey of efficiency techniques for adapting LLMs to scientific applications. Our review analyzes 120 studies across seven scientific fields, including biomedicine, clinical medicine, biology, mathematics, chemistry, geo-environmental science, and cross-domain scientific research. Across the surveyed literature, we summarize 34 representative models and 30 scientific datasets for efficient scientific LLM research. Examining parameter-efficient fine-tuning, knowledge distillation, architectural optimization, and data-centric approaches, we introduce a dual-axis taxonomy that organizes efficiency techniques by both methodological strategy and scientific domain. We further provide practical guidance for selecting efficiency strategies under resource constraints and highlight open challenges including multimodal integration, catastrophic forgetting, and automated method selection. By synthesizing cross-domain evidence and outlining directions for sustainable model development, this survey supports the adoption of efficient scientific LLMs in resource-constrained research environments and promotes more accessible and responsible deployment across scientific disciplines.

title: PresenceBench: An Exploratory Evaluation of Large Language Model Adaptation to User State
abstract: Presence-aware intelligence is the capacity of an AI system's intelligence layer to adapt appropriately to the functional state of the person it serves (here readiness, flow, and stability) while preserving task quality and safety. We introduce PresenceBench, an instrument for measuring it. PresenceBench evaluates how the intelligence layer uses a supplied state, not how that state is sensed, and breaks the capability into measurable properties. Two are tested here. Receptivity: does the model take up the state and give a better response than with no signal? Specificity: does any improvement depend on the correct state, rather than on extra structured context? A third, adaptation across states, is a required endpoint not measured in this release. A five-arm causal design answers both questions, against each model's own baseline and an equally structured mismatched-state control, scored by a correctness-gated human paired comparison. The exploratory evaluation covered four models across eighteen single-turn, six fixed three-turn and six simulated natural-conversation scenarios. Supplying a synthetic state, raw or translated into a response policy, gave human-preference point estimates above 0.5 for all four models (Claude Sonnet 5, DeepSeek V4 Pro, Gemini 3.6 Flash, GPT-5.6 Terra), with three of eight 95% intervals excluding chance. Specificity was not resolved: no per-model interval excluded chance, and the design cannot yet separate the state values from a generic instruction to adapt. Policy delivery reduced priced cost and output tokens against each model's baseline; these are resource-use changes, not efficiency gains, because correctness non-inferiority was not established. Safety-floor failures were rare (13 of 360 cases), with a non-significant excess under policy delivery. We report the instrument, the frozen results, and the controls a confirmatory study needs.
