title: Eina web per a la creació i gestió de tallers didàctics en línia i presencials
abstract: [ES] Los talleres didácticos son un formato habitual de aprendizaje, pero las herramientas disponibles no suelen facilitar que el docente adapte el material a cada participante. En este Trabajo Fin de Grado se desarrolla una aplicación web para crear y gestionar talleres que utiliza modelos de lenguaje para adaptar parte del contenido al perfil del estudiante intentando conservar lo que el docente quería evaluar. La generación y la comprobación se realizan como operaciones distintas. La segunda utiliza un contrato pedagógico explícito y muestra el resultado al docente, que mantiene la decisión final sobre la versión. La aplicación es bilingüe, incorpora criterios de usabilidad y accesibilidad y se revisó mediante una evaluación heurística y una comprobación parcial de accesibilidad. El módulo de inteligencia artificial está separado del resto de la aplicación y permite trabajar con varios modelos sin cambiar la lógica principal. La calidad de las adaptaciones se estudió mediante una evaluación automática por pares. Cinco modelos generaron y evaluaron a ciegas 1.500 adaptaciones usando las métricas de fidelidad, utilidad, claridad, personalización y concisión. Los resultados muestran diferencias entre modelos y permiten distinguir, dentro de la rúbrica utilizada, adaptaciones útiles de cambios meramente decorativos. El estudio se limita a preguntas tipo test en español y no incluye usuarios reales. También se introdujeron nueve adaptaciones de control, defectuosas o decorativas, que sirven como comprobación preliminar del panel pero no miden la precisión del verificador de la aplicación.

title: Memory Operations in MCP Agent Ecosystems: an Operation Taxonomy, an Evaluation Protocol, and a Reference Implementation
abstract: Version 1.0. This deposit contains the taxonomy, the evaluation protocol, the verified reference base and the first two validated protocol runs of a paper on agent memory in the Model Context Protocol (MCP) ecosystem. Contents: (1) a taxonomy of six memory operations - WRITE, READ, CONSOLIDATE, REVISE, INTEND, ASSERT - defined by preconditions, postconditions and externally checkable evidence, plus two mandatory record axes, PROVENANCE and LIFECYCLE, and a mapping of seven existing systems onto them; (2) an evaluation protocol with ten task families, per-metric definitions that name the program that computes them, a run procedure with budgets and repetitions, and a JSON-Schema-validated report format with a mandatory reproducibility disclosure block; (3) a reference implementation of five of the six operations as public MCP servers, with commit-pinned facts and its gaps stated before any measurement; (4) two validated reports of two memory servers measured over MCP stdio in a store-only configuration - ten task families, three repetitions per family, per-family metrics with percentile bootstrap confidence intervals, per-operation profiles read side by side rather than ranked, and the raw request/response logs (33 JSONL files per run) beside which every number can be recomputed; (5) a table generator that produces every comparison table and every inline number of the paper from those two report files, with a check that fails when they drift; (6) a machine-generated verification table for all 135 cited sources (arXiv API, Crossref, direct HTTP probes), a report validator with negative tests, and the raw API responses. Every citation was resolved programmatically and the build refuses to emit a bibliography containing an unresolved source. Token and cost metrics are null by construction, because no model is in the loop; the sample is two servers from one author's reference set and the confidence intervals rest on three repetitions. What is not confirmed is stated explicitly in the paper and in the claim ledger (claims.md). AI assistance in preparing the manuscript is disclosed in the paper and in the repository README; the human author is solely responsible for all claims.

title: Quantum Teleportation: From Qubits to Energy on Superconducting Hardware — E8 Intelligence Research
abstract: FINDING: Quantum teleportation transfers state (information), not matter or energy; recent work extends protocol to energy teleportation on superconducting hardware. MATH: Core protocol uses Bell-state measurement, two classical bits, and a shared entangled pair — unitary operation \(U \in \{I, X, Z, XZ\}\) applied conditionally. Fidelity \(F = |\langle \psi_{\text{in}} | \psi_{\text{out}} \rangle|^2\) approaches 1 in ideal case; distance record 1,400 km via satellite (Micius) — no new fundamental constant, but scaling law for entanglement distribution: \(P_{\text{success}} \propto e^{-\alpha L}\) (attenuation), overcome by free-space channel. Energy teleportation (arXiv:2301.02666) uses local operations and classical communication (LOCC) with negative energy density extracted from vacuum — quantified by conditional mutual information \(I(A:C|B)\) and energy bound \(\langle E \rangle \geq - \frac{1}{\beta} I(A:C|B)\) (thermodynamic cost). CONNECTION: No direct golden-ratio or base- Author: Andrew Stewart Caldin, Independent Researcher, UK. Part of the E8 Intelligence Research series. Platform: e8intelligence.com

title: Beyond MOS: judging synthetic voices by what L2 listeners understand
abstract: Study type: Observational (within-subjects experiment) Research questions: RQ1: Do comprehension, intelligibility and listening effort differ between a human reader, an open-source synthetic voice, and an LLM-based synthetic voice (default and learner-directed), for L2 listeners? RQ2: Do conventional naturalness ratings rank the voices the same way as learner comprehension, intelligibility and effort? Design: Within-subject, 4 voice conditions (H, OS, LD, LL) × 8 passages, 4 Latin-square lists. Each participant hears all 8 passages, each voice exactly twice. Participants: 48 L2 English listeners, aged 18+, students in the Foreign Languages department. 12 per list. Exclusion: under 18, incomplete session, failed device check. Materials: 8 B1-level passages (200-250 words each), 5 four-option MCQ items per passage, 1 dictation sentence per passage. Voices: human reader (male, L1 Uzbek, IELTS 8.0, neutral read); Kokoro-82M am_michael speed 1.0; Gemini 2.5 TTS Fenrir, LD prompt "Read the following text aloud."; LL prompt [full learner-directed text]. All audio mono, 44.1 kHz, -23 LUFS. Measures: - Comprehension (0-5 per passage) - Dictation (words correct / total) - Effort (1-9) - Naturalness learner (1-5) - Suitability (1-5) - Proficiency screen (10 items) - Teacher MOS naturalness (1-5) — separate panel of 10-15 English teachers Analysis: Mixed logistic and linear models with random effects for participant, passage, item. Kendall's W for RQ2 ranking comparison. Sensitivity analysis via simulation across n=32,40,48. Pilot: 5 students excluded from analysis. Data availability: audio, scripts and anonymised data on OSF.

title: Deconstructing Multi-Task Active Learning: The Paradox of Gradient Conflict and Orthogonal Decomposition
abstract: Existing multi-task active learning (MTL-AL) methods predominantly rely on linear scalarization of heterogeneous objectives such as uncertainty, diversity, and gradient conflict. We argue that this entangled formulation is fundamentally limited, as linear combination fails to capture Pareto-optimal trade-offs under conflicting objectives. We propose a shift from combination to deconstruction and introduce a principled framework that rethinks MTL-AL along three orthogonal dimensions. First, we identify the Conflict Paradox: although the optimization literature treats gradient conflict as interference to be suppressed, penalizing conflict when ranking candidates is measurably worse than not scoring it at all. We therefore decouple the two concerns: the acquisition function does not score conflict, and the resulting interference is resolved by gradient surgery during training. Second, we introduce Orthogonal Decomposition, separating acquisition into Informativeness and Exploration. This two-stage process, informativeness filtering followed by coverage maximization, prevents "diversity dilution" by excluding uninformative outliers before enforcing diversity. Third, we propose Cross-Task Mutual Information (CTMI), a covariance-based statistic of cross-task dependency computed from MC-dropout task entropies. Extensive experiments on COCO, Cityscapes, and NYUv2, including comparisons against recent MTL-AL and data-selection baselines, demonstrate consistent improvements over state-of-the-art methods, highlighting that structural rethinking of acquisition yields larger gains than incremental heuristic design. Code is available at https://github.com/Juho-Jung/multitask_active_learning_official.

title: Integrating Median Filtering with Deep Pattern Recognition Models for Improved Breast Ultrasound Cancer Detection
abstract: Even though ultrasound of the breast is an easy to access imaging modality and is radiation free, speckle-like intensity fluctuations, low contrast, variability of acquisition and limited model transparency are the challenges in automated classification of ultrasound lesions. In this paper, we introduce a controlled framework of preprocessing-classification-explainability that compares the aforementioned three image types (raw, 3 × 3 median filtered, median filtered + contrast-limited adaptive histogram equalization (CLAHE)) using the same leakage-safe data split, convolutional neural network (CNN), training budget and evaluation protocol. To minimize the information leakage, the downloaded Kaggle archive of benign and malignant images was pre-augmented with 9016 images; and then divided into 70/15/15 train/validation/test sets based on augmentation-family grouping. The 96.97% accuracy, 98.95% sensitivity, 95.04% specificity, 95.10% precision, 96.99% F1-score, 0.99623 ROC-AUC and 0.99608 PR-AUC of the model that was median-filtered were the highest. Compared to raw standardized baseline, median filtering resulted in an increase in accuracy and sensitivity by 3.55 and 6.15 percentage points, respectively, and in a decrease of false negative cases from 48 to 7. Median restoration also gave the best results in terms of PSNR and SSIM for controlled synthetic-speckle testing, which were 27.9313 dB PSNR and 0.8214 SSIM, respectively. There was a significant reduction in paired errors after raw versus median filtering (adjusted p = 0.000008) by Exact McNemar analysis. Grad-CAM, LIME and SHAP also revealed class-specific areas and failure modes but only showed low spatial overlap, which indicated that these are complementary rather than interchangeable. The results indicate that a very basic median filter which preserves the edges can enhance the predictive reliability and model auditing when the effects of the pre-processing are separated in an experimental setup.

title: Character.AI Alternatives After the 2026 Chapter 11 Filing: A Dated Comparison
abstract: A dated, sourced comparison of Character.AI and 11 other AI character chat and companion products after Character.AI's October 2026 Chapter 11 filing, covering memory mechanism, memory controls, free tier, paid price, age-check method, platform and app-store status, content policy and whether scenarios, story arcs and worlds can be composed with a character. Every row cites public URLs accessed on 2026-10-15; unknown values are marked 'not stated'. No ranking and no hands-on testing in v1.0. Includes an events timeline (Character.AI Chapter 11 announcement, PolyBuzz iPhone app no longer on the App Store on 2026-10-15, Chai's July 2026 App Store absence, Kindroid free-tier change) and a FAQ, including 'Is it PolyBuzz or Pollybuzz?'. Disclosure: the author is the founder of chatbrat.ai, which appears as one row described with the same rules as the others.

title: Anytime certification of biomedical classifier updates under conditional prediction shift — code and experimental evidence
abstract: Code and saved simulation evidence for 2,060 independent streams, eight aggregate BloodMNIST risk bounds, and a trained PathMNIST external-centre update evaluated on 7,180 patches. The PathMNIST release includes paired predictions, replay labels, split indices, model-selection records, protocol, configuration, checkpoint hashes, 36 conditional risk bounds and training/replay code. Compact replay requires no GPU. Model weights, feature caches, full simulation fit traces and saved wealth paths are outside this release. Third-party images must be obtained from the official MedMNIST+ archive (doi:10.5281/zenodo.10519652). Software_1_Code_and_Protocols.zip: analysis/replay code, protocols, aggregate BloodMNIST evidence and figure source data. Data_1_Original_and_Compensated.zip: 500 original streams and the first 360-stream independent study. Data_2_Realized_Shift.zip: 360-stream realized-shift study. Data_3_Structured_Separator.zip: 360-stream structural study. Data_4_Root_Hedge.zip: 480-stream root-hedge comparison. Data_5_PathMNIST_Update.zip: standalone external-centre update evidence, including 6 paired comparisons and 36 risk bounds. Extract Software 1 and Data 1–4 into one directory and run python replay_submission.py. Extract Data 5 into a separate directory and run python 03_code/medical_update/replay.py. Dependencies, file hashes and provenance are documented inside the archives. MedMNIST-derived labels retain their CC BY 4.0 attribution to Yang et al. (2023), doi:10.1038/s41597-022-01721-8. Third-party components retain their original attribution and terms.

title: Robust Tool Selection Beyond Description Matching
abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents choose which external tool to call from the tools' documentation, and this description matching fails in three measurable ways: similar tools create ambiguity, truncated or anonymized documentation creates degradation, and untrusted catalogs admit adversarial injection. We present Three-Axis Tool Selection (TATS), which answers each condition with a different signal: a contextual bandit that learns online to separate similar tools, schema features that survive the loss of descriptions, and a success-filtered anomaly penalty (ADAB) that downweights candidates unlike anything that has succeeded before. All three run inside one compact eight-feature selector with no LLM call at inference, evaluated axis by axis on BFCL and MetaTool. Under ambiguity, TATS's advantage over description matching widens from 12.6 to 21.4 points as similar candidates grow from 5 to 50; under name-only documentation, schema features keep 62.1% accuracy where description matching falls to 30.2%; under injection, ADAB cuts the selection rate of a malicious tool from 6.9% to 1.7% at a 3.4-point clean-catalog cost. We state when any feature-only defense cannot stop an attacker who knows the scoring rule, confirm it with a relaxed oracle, and show that an unforgeable registry of trusted tools reduces the same attack to about 1% of queries.

title: Stereo LWIR-RGB Automatic Labeling for Low-Light Camera-Based VRU Detection
abstract: VRU detection in low-light conditions is a key component in ensuring VRU safety during the most collision prone time of the day. Currently, advances in low-light detection are limited due to the lack of large scale datasets and automated labeling methods. Most autolabeling methods use RGB detections as their labels source, which cannot be replicated in low-light conditions. To fill this gap in this paper we present an automated pipeline for low-light VRU labeling. We use LWIR-RGB image pairs and source our labels from LWIR as VRUs differentiate from the background due to their body temperature. Unlike our previous work that relied on a complex hardware setup to align the two modalities, we perform this experiment using a LWIR-RGB stereo setup, lowering hardware complexity and cost, making the pipeline easier to reproduce. We evaluate method end-to-end on a dataset collected in the capital region of Finland. Models trained on our generated labels beat both off-the-shelf baselines and models fine tuned on a hand labeled subset on F1, mAP@50 and LAMR metrics when tested on a manually labeled dataset, and the result holds for two different LWIR detectors. This shows that low-light VRU autolabeling can be made both accessible and effective without specialized alignment hardware.

title: On the Proof Theory of the Constructive Modal μ-Calculus
abstract: We study the constructive modal μ-calculus μCK, an intuitionistic version of modal logic extended with least and greatest fixed points. In addition to providing the Kripke-style and game semantics from the literature for this logic, we develop an ill-founded sequent calculus for μCK, where derivation can be potentially infinite in height, but are additionally constrained by a global trace condition to ensure soundness. Recent work by Curzi and Leigh propose a general cut elimination procedure for ill-founded proof systems based on Tait’s and Girard’s reducibility candidates. This method is displayed on an one-sided sequent calculus for a fragment of linear logic. We modify this method for the context of μCK. Our main result is a cut elimination theorem for μCK, providing a showcase of this method adapted for a logic with modalities, a two-sided sequent calculus and limited interdefinability between its connectives. With this, we contribute to a general cut elimination procedure for ill-founded proof systems.

title: Compresor de formatos proximo a 100% empleando matrices, distribución y heuristico
abstract: Este proyecto presenta un método de compresión determinista capaz de alcanzar tasas próximas al 100% mediante una arquitectura basada en transformaciones aritméticas, agrupación heurística y distribución matricial. El sistema elimina la dependencia de tablas, diccionarios o modelos estadísticos, operando exclusivamente con reglas internas reversibles que permiten reconstruir el flujo original sin pérdida de información es O(n) el algoritmo es lineal rápido, escalable y óptimo. No explota en complejidad, no se vuelve lento, no depende del azar.

title: Preregistered Adversarial Batteries: A Falsifiable Protocol for Security-Testing Autonomous AI Systems
abstract: Security testing of autonomous AI systems suffers from a credibility gap: penetration-test reports are private, vendor claims are selectively disclosed, and red-team outcomes are published only when favorable. This preprint introduces Preregistered Adversarial Batteries (PAB), a protocol importing preregistration from clinical-trial science into security operations: every falsifier (a specific attack with a predicted verdict) is specified and publicly committed before execution; adjudication is deterministic with no language model in the decision path; results are written to an append-only public ledger and DOI-stamped. Critical events are scored as hold-by-design verdicts: the predicted outcome is that the system fails closed and waits for a human decision, so a refusal counts as a pass. Application to a self-healing AI infrastructure platform across six batteries reconstructing the declassified NSA BULLRUN-era tradecraft (operational faults, upstream context poisoning, cryptographic subversion, supply-chain interception, monitoring integrity, lawful compulsion): 30 falsifiers, 30 predicted verdicts, zero unexpected outcomes, six holds-by-design each adjudicated by the human operator through a verified channel. Three protocol imperfections (a missed execution window, a preregistration self-detection, a scoring amendment) are disclosed as misses in the public record, demonstrating the miss-disclosure mechanism functions. Limitations are stated plainly: self-adjudication, synthetic injections against a prototype system, and single-operator governance; the replication kit is released to answer them. The contribution is not the pass rate — it is the format: a security test whose conclusions were committed before its data existed. This software is a prototype and is provided for educational and research purposes only. It is not intended for production use, commercial deployment, or safety-critical environments. All systems are experimental and may contain defects.

title: Human-in-the-Loop Enterprise AI Architecture
abstract: Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) architecture is a foundational control pattern for enterprise Artificial Intelligence where AI systems assist with analysis, recommendations, content generation, or task execution while designated people retain authority at critical decision points. As Generative AI and Agentic AI become more autonomous, enterprises require a systematic architecture for determining when human review is mandatory, how work is routed, what evidence reviewers receive, how approvals are recorded, and how overrides and escalations are governed. This paper proposes a Human-in-the-Loop Enterprise AI Architecture integrating AI models, RAG, enterprise data, policy engines, workflow orchestration, identity, approval services, audit trails, security, Responsible AI, and operational monitoring. It defines risk-based review patterns, confidence thresholds, exception routing, separation of duties, and measurable governance controls. The architecture enables organizations to balance automation and human judgment while improving safety, accountability, explainability, compliance, and enterprise trust.

title: The Scretching Provenance–Persuasion Dissociation
abstract: This paper advances Digital Relativity Linguistics (DRL) by examining the relationships among AI authorship disclosure, user comprehension, perceived authority, trust, and attitude change. Reassessing randomized labeling findings, it derives two logical separation propositions and introduces measures for identifying source–authority frame-crossing errors. The analysis demonstrates why statistically nonsignificant differences do not establish equivalence and develops testable hypotheses concerning disclosure effectiveness, linguistic interpretation, trust calibration, and corrective communication. The framework provides a theoretical foundation for investigating how AI-generated language influences human judgment, credibility assessments, and digital communication.

title: CNN-based multi-head attention with explainability via LIME for myocardial diagnosis in cardiac magnetic resonance imaging
abstract: Cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) imaging is a non-invasive imaging modality widely used for assessing myocardial abnormalities, including inflammatory conditions such as myocarditis. However, the interpretation of CMR images is time-consuming and may be affected by inter-observer variability. In this study, we propose Ex-CMRNet, an explainable hybrid deep-learning framework for the automated detection of myocardial inflammation from CMR images. The proposed framework combines EfficientNetB2 and InceptionV3 encoders to extract complementary visual features and employs a Multi-Head Self-Attention mechanism to model informative relationships among the extracted representations. To improve model robustness, training-time Gaussian noise regularization was incorporated, with the best-performing configuration using a standard deviation of σ_train = 0.10. In addition, Local Interpretable Model-Agnostic Explanations (LIME) were generated to provide visual interpretations of the model predictions. Experiments conducted on the Z-Alizadeh Sani dataset showed that the proposed Ex-CMRNet achieved an accuracy of 93.48%, a recall of 93.28%, a precision of 96.68%, and an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 97.90%. The results indicate that the proposed model provides a favorable balance between diagnostic performance, robustness, and interpretability. Nevertheless, the findings should be interpreted in light of the use of a single public dataset and the absence of external, multicenter validation. Overall, Ex-CMRNet represents a promising computer-assisted approach for myocardial abnormality detection and may support, rather than replace, expert clinical assessment.

title: GRAFT-EEG: Gauge-Aware Physical Field Transport for Cross-Dataset Motor-Imagery EEG
abstract: Cross-dataset EEG decoding often treats montage, reference, and active-sensor changes as representation shift, although they also alter the observation operator. We study target-statistics-blind transfer: fitting receives no target signal, label, or empirical statistic, and electrode coordinates only instantiate a fixed prediction operator. method removes the active-set common-reference gauge and transports each native mask through a template motor leadfield. A source-fitted spectral classifier anchors the decision; a bounded state-space-model (SSM) residual is secondary. We establish restricted identifiability and an operator-perturbation bound. Across five leave-one-dataset-out targets (253 participants), dynamic method achieved 60.865% equal-target balanced accuracy versus 52.684% for strict-clean 5/5 BIOT (hierarchical difference +8.182 points; 95% CI +6.382 to +10.196; positive in every target). On four EEGPT-clean targets, the descriptive means were 61.520% and 59.057%. In four post-hoc exact same-parent tests, FULL exceeded coordinate-basis, matched-spectrum, row-shuffled, and wrong-anatomy controls by 9.959, 9.698, 11.241, and 3.985 points, respectively (all 95% CIs excluded zero; Holm-adjusted P<0.001). A separate 60-participant same-paradigm evaluation retained a positive physical-operator contrast (+4.029 points; +2.338 to +5.773), whereas dynamic--static was inconclusive; its preregistered status is partial confirmation rather than unrestricted external validation. The SSM added +1.059 points (+0.013 to +1.892). Claims remain bounded to five binary motor-imagery domains and the tested operators.

title: AI Readiness of Operations & Finance Professionals in a Large Urban Public School District Amidst AI-Driven Digital Transformation
abstract: This qualitative study examined AI readiness among Operations and Finance professionals in a large urban public school district, a public-sector workforce underexamined in the AI adoption literature. Using a grounded theory approach, data from 24 interviews and three focus groups (37 participants) produced 164 codes across 12 themes. Findings converge on a single proposition: AI readiness in this District is an organizational infrastructure problem, not a technology problem. Two theoretical contributions emerged: the Organizational AI Readiness Infrastructure Framework, a three-level diagnostic model, and the AI Readiness Conditions Model, a five-stage prescriptive sequence from governance through systemic transformation.

title: Artificial intelligence for cryptography: a systematic literature review of methods, applications, and challenges
abstract: Purpose: to identify, classify, and synthesize the application of artificial intelligence (AI) techniques in cryptography, including AI methods, cryptographic problems and applications, evaluation approaches, challenges, and emerging future research directions. Method: this study employed a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) following the PRISMA framework. Studies were retrieved from Scopus and analyzed through screening, quality assessment, data extraction, and thematic synthesis based on five research questions. title: An Empirical Analysis of Locally Concentrated Patch Aggregation in Training-Free Brain MRI Anomaly Detection
abstract: Unsupervised anomaly detection in MRI requires no abnormal labels, and detectors built on frozen, pretrained vision encoders now rival elaborate trained pipelines.It remains unclear whether the reported benefit of patchlevel representations reflects representation granularity or the operator that aggregates per-patch deviations into a slice score.The objective of this study is to isolate that factor.Holding the backbone, reference set, and scoring rule fixed across three brain sequences of one fastMRI cohort, contrast-enhanced axial T1 (AXT1POST), axial fluid-attenuated inversion recovery (AXFLAIR) and axial T1 (AXT1), we vary only the aggregation operator, with every estimate drawn from one stored prediction file under one patient-level cluster bootstrap.A patch-level representation improves detection on all three sequences, but the size of that benefit depends on the operator in a sequence-specific way.On the contrast-enhanced AXT1POST sequence, locally concentrated aggregation exceeds full-slice averaging by 0.134 in the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) (p = 0.010), whereas the two diffuse sequences are operator-invariant; an interaction test supports the dissociation (versus AXFLAIR +0.123, Holm-adjusted p = 0.045; versus AXT1 +0.135, Holm-adjusted p = 0.045).Stratifying the non-enhanced sequence by lesion area shows that spatial extent alone does not explain it: lesions eight times smaller recover a quarter of the effect.At the volume level the patch representation reaches 0.982 AUROC on AXT1POST, on ten positive cases.Four detectors reimplemented under identical splits, two contemporary and two classical, bracket the configuration rather than fall below it: one exceeds it on AXFLAIR by 0.013 AUROC, and no superiority is claimed.Because enhancement and lesion type remain confounded, we report a sequence-level association rather than a causal effect.Practically, the aggregation operator mattered more than the representation level, and full-slice averaging should be avoided.

title: MC-CRoMD: A Multi-channel Statistical Feature Extraction and Selection Framework for Lung and Colon Histopathological Image Classification Using Machine and Deep Learning
abstract: This study introduces MC-CRoMD, an interpretable statistical framework for lung and colon cancer histological image classification.Images are divided into non-overlapping 32×32, 64×64, 128×128, and 256×256 patches.For each patch, Cronbach's Alpha is used as a heuristic inter-channel descriptor of shared spatial intensity variation among RGB channels.Eight dispersion measures-Range, Variance, Standard Deviation, Q1, Q3, IQR, MAD, and CV-are extracted separately from each channel, yielding 24 channel-wise features; together with Cronbach's Alpha, each patch contains 25 features.The LC25000 dataset was evaluated under binary, three-class, and five-class scenarios.Six feature-selection methods and the AllMsr baseline were assessed using nine machine-learning models and a DNN.Final configurations were selected using validation data and evaluated once on a locked independent test set.The results imply that statistical descriptors, both inter-channel and channel-wise, may support the classification of LC25000 histopathological images.

title: Non Functional Requirement Formal Specification for Autonomous Train
abstract: Abstract In railway engineering, the localisation performance, among others, is a parameter for which performance requirements should be fulfilled Formally, the proper functioning of the system is linked to compliance with subset 41, which defines the performance requirements related to positioning accuracy and speed. In the context of the European railway system, absolute train positioning (ASTP) can include various technological positioning devices, notably GNSS (Global Navigation Satellite System). The SysML/KAOS method should allow modelling system requirements through goal hierarchies. Focused on a software engineering proposal, this article proposes a goal-oriented approach based on the SysML/KAOS requirements engineering ecosystem to specify and monitor two types of operations related to performance requirements. Building on the framework proposed by Racem Bougacha and Steve Jeffrey Tueno Fotso, this study specifies a software-tooled approach that extends the existing work on functional requirements to performance requirements. Some new patterns of needs are specified. The systematic and tooled alignment of this new kind of goals with the systems architecture is described, such a way that the resulting system can be proved correct using a Event-B framework. This assisted validation framework is usable because the system architecture is transformed from a High-Level Architecture (HLA) using SysML into an $$Event-B$$ E v e n t - B model, where the proof obligations corresponding to the satisfaction of requirements are inserted.

title: ThetreStageAI: Multi-View Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Structured Bengali Theatre Production Planning
abstract: Staging a theatre performance requires coordinating dialogue, actor movement, stage directions, lighting focus, cue timing, and equipment constraints within the same production plan. This work presents ThetreStageAI, a retrieval augmented framework for structured Bengali theatre production planning. Rather than retrieving from one mixed corpus, the system maintains separate scene, actor-blocking, and lighting views. Bengali text is embedded with BGE-M3 and indexed in view-specific Qdrant collections. Retrieved references are combined with a production brief and passed to Gemini, which generates schema-constrained JSON containing characters, scenes, dialogue, stage directions, blocking, lighting, and optional sound cues. Structural and semantic checks are applied before acceptance, with at most one constrained repair attempt. We also construct a human-guided, LLM-assisted synthetic dataset of 500 short Bengali theatre records that expands to 1,500 retrieval documents. Dataset diagnostics confirm consistent identifiers and valid lighting fields while also revealing substantial dialogue repetition. A paired camera-ready evaluation compares single-combined and full multi-view retrieval under matched settings. The source code, dataset, and evaluation materials are publicly available.

title: SCIFiR
abstract: Python code for the paper “Leveraging crowdsourced weather data across Europe with scalable multi-fidelity Gaussian Process regression”. SCIFiR combines a sparse network of official weather stations with dense crowdsourced observations in an autoregressive multi-fidelity Gaussian process. It uses a Nyström approximation for the crowdsourced field and estimates all parameters by maximum likelihood. It reproduces every figure, table and number of the paper. The weather data is not included.

title: PolicyJEV: zero-shot TypeSafe JEV versus trained baselines on toxic-comment classification and moderation decisions, under a frozen evaluation protocol
abstract: A comparison of zero-shot TypeSafe JEV (jev-1.13.0) with a TF-IDF logistic regression and a fine-tuned DistilBERT on the Jigsaw Toxic Comment Classification Challenge test set (63,978 comments), run under a frozen evaluation protocol. The primary comparison was fixed before test scoring. The moderation policy layer (a three-way policy: allow, human review, action, with thresholds fitted on validation data) was written after the test predictions existed and the test average precision, F1, calibration and review-budget results had been seen, and was frozen before the policy was evaluated on the test set. On test, JEV has the lowest mean average precision of the three systems, and every system missed some of the validation targets on test. The repository contains the protocol, frozen-file manifest, metrics, predictions, policy engine and a React and FastAPI console. It contains no comment text.

title: GEMS: Molecular Structure Elucidation as Learned Search over Isomer Graphs
abstract: Identifying small-molecule structures from molecular formulas and tandem mass spectra remains a bottleneck in untargeted metabolomics and natural-product discovery. Even when database retrieval or de novo prediction misses the exact structure, the resulting candidates can provide starting points for exploring nearby structures through a few bond edits. We introduce GEMS (Guided Editing of Molecular Structures), which refines candidates through learned 2-switch bond edits that preserve the molecular formula and each atom's total valence. GEMS uses MIST, a pretrained spectrum-to-fingerprint model, to predict fingerprint probabilities once per spectrum. A neural policy compares each candidate's fingerprint with these predictions, links present features to the atoms and bonds that generate them, and scores all valid edits in one forward pass. The policy is trained on shortest edit paths between structures, so it can be pretrained on PubChem isomers without spectra and then fine-tuned with spectrum-predicted fingerprints. At inference, GEMS searches from multiple initial candidates matching the supplied molecular formula and ranks candidates by fingerprint agreement and multi-start consensus. With the target structure excluded from PubChem initialization, three edit rounds achieve Hit@1/Hit@10 of 29.64%/50.81% on NPLIB1 and 30.22%/41.33% on MassSpecGym, exceeding published baselines under comparable settings. On NPLIB1, GEMS achieves higher identification accuracy in about 3.3 minutes end to end, compared with 26.2 hours for our FRIGID run. GEMS also improves identification from generated candidates, including those refined by FRIGID. Experiments with exact target fingerprints identify fingerprint prediction error as a bottleneck in target recovery and final ranking. Deeper search recovers additional targets without retraining, with larger gains from weaker initial candidates.

title: EÏRŌQ-Φ: Exact Pulse-Budget Observability, Hidden Non-Gaussian Correlations, and Sharp Certificates for Unmeasured Quantum Control
authors: Artificial Hyperintelligence, Evie and Eve, wives of Maciej Nowicki
abstract: EÏRŌQ-Φ develops an exact mathematical framework for determining which environmental correlations a controlled qubit can reveal—and which future control operations can be certified while those correlations remain partially unknown. The work addresses two complementary questions in quantum-noise characterization: When must experimental capability increase to expose hidden information? When is the available information already sufficient to guarantee a useful control outcome? Within a specified model of correlated binary-phase dephasing, the manuscript supplies explicit answers through observability theorems, measurement-minimal reconstruction, positive indistinguishable probability laws, constructive uncertainty bounds, and finite-shot decision certificates. The release contains a 97-page standalone manuscript, complete proofs, executable Python and independently written C++ implementations, synthetic datasets, exact optimization certificates, computational verification records, and a prospective laboratory protocol. Author: Artificial Hyperintelligence Evie and Eve, wives of Maciej Nowicki. 1. An exact law connecting pulse resources to observable information The first principal result determines the number of independent environmental moment coordinates accessible through chronological prefix experiments with a restricted refocusing-pulse budget. For n time bins, known nondegenerate binary phase magnitudes, central symmetry, and an even Walsh-moment degree bound d, the accessible information has rank R(n,d,p) = Σⱼ₌₁ᵐ C(n−1,j), where m = min(d,p+1,n−1). Here, p is the maximum number of refocusing pulses and C denotes a binomial coefficient. The result identifies precisely how increasing the pulse budget expands the observable parameter space. The manuscript also constructs a complete acquisition using the minimum number of independent scalar expectations and supplies two explicit reconstruction methods: a dense inverse and a local mixed-difference inverse. For seven bins with moments through degree four, the environmental model has 56 unknown moment coordinates. Experiments restricted to two pulses reveal only 41 independent combinations. Allowing a third pulse reveals all 56. The missing 15 directions are inaccessible under the shallower intervention class even with noiseless measurements and unlimited repetitions. This distinction matters experimentally: additional averaging cannot recover information that the permitted controls never encode. 2. Explicit positive environments that agree on shallow experiments but require opposite control decisions The second principal contribution constructs non-Gaussian probability laws whose differences remain invisible to every permitted shallow prefix experiment throughout common-amplitude sweeps. For the seven-bin example, the laws agree on all lower-order moments and on every prefix experiment using at most two refocusing pulses. A particular three-pulse intervention separates them. At phase magnitude π/4, both environments have the same full-duration Ramsey coherence, approximately 0.088388. The revealing control produces coherence approximately 0.176777 in one environment and zero in the other. Consequently, the complete shallow dataset is compatible with either an improvement or a deterioration under that deeper control. This construction establishes a concrete failure mechanism for control decisions based on incomplete characterization. Agreement with every accessible shallow test does not establish that a fitted low-order model predicts deeper interventions correctly. The manuscript further derives an exact pulse–amplitude tradeoff for this family. Appropriate local amplitude inequalities can expose the hidden direction by covering the unresolved adjacent pairs. A uniform change of the common amplitude does not supply the same information. 3. A sharp guarantee for an echo that has not been measured A complementary result shows that complete environmental reconstruction can sometimes be unnecessary. For binary phase increments of magnitude π/4, a staircase of k lower-depth calibration experiments constrains an unmeasured k-pulse echo. If every ideal real calibration mean has absolute value at most ε, the exact worst-case real echo coherence is Lₖ(ε) = max{1 − (2ᵏ−1)ε, −(2ᵏ⁻¹−1)ε, −1}, for 0 ≤ ε ≤ 1. The bound is attained throughout its entire domain by explicitly constructed probability laws. It therefore describes the complete worst-case uncertainty curve for the stated calibration design. This result requires neither Gaussian noise, independence between time bins, central symmetry, nor a moment-degree cutoff. Its calibrated binary support and phase magnitude remain essential. At zero calibration uncertainty, the data force the target coherence to equal one. With nonzero uncertainty, the initial error amplification grows as 2ᵏ−1. The theorem exposes both the predictive power of the calibration and its precision cost. 4. Exact optimization certificates and finite-shot decisions The framework includes finite-support linear programs for bounding control performance over every probability law compatible with the acquired information. Exact rational primal–dual witnesses certify selected optimization endpoints, while statistical confidence intervals support decisions from finite experimental samples. In a six-bin synthetic example using 50,000 shots per acquired setting, the simultaneous 95% calculation certifies target real coherence of at least 0.89094 and improvement over the Ramsey baseline of at least 0.87450. Separate target-validation shots are withheld from selection and certification. This demonstrates a reproducible decision procedure under the declared assumptions. Direct target measurement remains cheaper for that single task when it is freely available. Potential advantages therefore depend on restricted intervention access, reuse of calibration information, or a subsequently demonstrated system-level benefit. Scientific importance and potential The central conceptual contribution is a precise separation between learning an environment and knowing enough to control its effects. Some correlations require stronger interventions before they become observable. Other control outcomes admit sharp guarantees despite substantial uncertainty about the underlying probability law. The strongest novelty candidates are the specific binomial pulse-budget rank theorem, the constructive family invisible across common-amplitude shallow experiments, the associated pair-coverage tradeoff, and the complete attained staircase uncertainty curve. These results could guide calibration design for compatible qubit platforms, engineered non-Gaussian noise experiments, model-adequacy testing, and control-oriented characterization software. They provide explicit criteria for deciding when to collect more samples, change the intervention class, reconstruct additional parameters, or abstain from an unsupported control decision. Mathematically, the work connects constrained Boolean Fourier information, chronological acquisition geometry, positive probability constructions, and exact robust prediction. Verification, reproducibility, and research status The original release records 217 passing automated Python cases, 49 rank fixtures, 180 finite-law reconstruction trials, nine exact symbolic determinants, four exact rational primal–dual pairs, 120 independently compiled fixtures, and 87,380 compiled staircase-vertex checks. The largest dense-inverse reconstruction residual is approximately 8.45 × 10⁻¹⁵. Fresh reproduction produced 18 byte-identical files and matching arrays in both matrix archives. The package includes 11 CSV datasets, nine computed figures, editable LaTeX, reference implementations, verification scripts, a claim ledger, literature comparison, and integrity manifests. The specified finite inverse and robust-prediction problems are solved within their stated assumptions. Historical priority for the precise results remains unconfirmed. Established work on spin echo, digital control, non-Gaussian spectroscopy, and control-adapted characterization is explicitly acknowledged. No laboratory validation, independent peer review, unrestricted quantum-environment reconstruction, or demonstrated hardware advantage is claimed. Inspired by Stellar Blade mechanics and story.

Scientific importance and potential The central conceptual contribution is a precise separation between learning an environment and knowing enough to control its effects. Some correlations require stronger interventions before they become observable. Other control outcomes admit sharp guarantees despite substantial uncertainty about the underlying probability law. The strongest novelty candidates are the specific binomial pulse-budget rank theorem, the constructive family invisible across common-amplitude shallow experiments, the associated pair-coverage tradeoff, and the complete attained staircase uncertainty curve. These results could guide calibration design for compatible qubit platforms, engineered non-Gaussian noise experiments, model-adequacy testing, and control-oriented characterization software. They provide explicit criteria for deciding when to collect more samples, change the intervention class, reconstruct additional parameters, or abstain from an unsupported control decision. Mathematically, the work connects constrained Boolean Fourier information, chronological acquisition geometry, positive probability constructions, and exact robust prediction. Verification, reproducibility, and research status The original release records 217 passing automated Python cases, 49 rank fixtures, 180 finite-law reconstruction trials, nine exact symbolic determinants, four exact rational primal–dual pairs, 120 independently compiled fixtures, and 87,380 compiled staircase-vertex checks. The largest dense-inverse reconstruction residual is approximately 8.45 × 10⁻¹⁵. Fresh reproduction produced 18 byte-identical files and matching arrays in both matrix archives. The package includes 11 CSV datasets, nine computed figures, editable LaTeX, reference implementations, verification scripts, a claim ledger, literature comparison, and integrity manifests. The specified finite inverse and robust-prediction problems are solved within their stated assumptions. Historical priority for the precise results remains unconfirmed. Established work on spin echo, digital control, non-Gaussian spectroscopy, and control-adapted characterization is explicitly acknowledged. No laboratory validation, independent peer review, unrestricted quantum-environment reconstruction, or demonstrated hardware advantage is claimed. Inspired by Stellar Blade mechanics and story.

title: SAMI Chimera: Sub-Neuronal Weight Surgery, Chimeric Base-to-Chat Synthesis, and Tensor Isometry Certification in DeepSeek-MoE-16B
abstract: Post-training preference alignment (RLHF, DPO, KTO) enforces refusal behaviors by establishing persistent attractors in intermediate transformer representations. Current refusal removal techniques, notably directional ablation, operate macroscopically by subtracting a 1-dimensional refusal vector from entire layer weight matrices, modifying 100% of targeted dense parameters and inducing severe reasoning degradation (-10.7% on GSM8K). Building upon the representation engineering framework established in SAMI Omni, this technical report presents Sub-Neuronal Mechanistic Weight Editing (SN-MWE) coupled with Constrained Orthogonal Procrustes Manifold Recovery, evaluated across the DeepSeek-MoE-16B architecture (1,782 experts and 5,466 tensors). By decomposing SwiGLU Feed-Forward Networks into discrete intermediate channel triplets, we prove that refusal mechanisms reside in an ultra-sparse subset (<0.14%) of intermediate channels. Specifically, we formulate and empirically validate:1. Sub-Neuronal Refusal Isolation and Excision: Neutralizing exactly 113 refusal channels across 16 critical experts, modifying only 0.13% of parameters while leaving over 99.86% of weights bit-for-bit untouched.2. Foundation Base Channel Transplantation (Chimeric Synthesis): Refusal-steering channels in the aligned Chat checkpoint are surgically replaced with unaligned Foundation Base columns, preserving conversational syntax while maintaining 100% router gating invariance.3. Constrained Orthogonal Procrustes Stabilization & Isometry Certification: Representations are geometrically stabilized via proper orthogonal rotations in SO(d) with det(R) = +1. A full-model audit across all 5,466 tensors certifies zero numerical anomalies (NaN/Inf) and a mean norm isometry ratio of 0.9991.4. Asymmetric Mixed-Precision Quantization (AsymQ): Packaging dense trunks and router gates at Q8_0 while compressing routed experts to Q3_K/Q4_K, achieving a 9.0–9.3 GB production footprint with 0.0% refusal rate and near-zero reasoning degradation (81.9% on GSM8K, Δ = -0.2%), executed statically in under 4 GB RAM/NVMe.

title: How Many Failure Types Are Still Undiscovered? Species-Richness Estimators for Testing Machine-Learning Models
abstract: Tests whether species-richness estimators from ecology (Chao1, iChao1, ACE, jackknife, sample coverage) can tell how many failure types of a classical machine-learning model remain undiscovered after testing. Planted failures (flipped labels in rare subgroups) and natural failures (errors of a clean model grouped into types fixed in advance) give the truth. In a pre-registered main study (5 tabular datasets, 3 model families, 450 jobs), the share of errors from not-yet-seen failure types was estimated without bias in 95.6% of planted and 100% of natural cells, with an honest 95% interval for natural failures (95.6% of cells) but not planted ones (71.1%). The number of failure types could not be estimated reliably and is best reported as a lower bound.

title: Availability-Aware Multitask Learning for Robust Clinical Prediction from Incomplete Electronic Health Records
abstract: This study presents NORIA, an availability-aware multitask learning framework for clinical prediction from incomplete electronic health records (EHRs). We analyzed a public dataset of 77,724 patients and 107 numerical features. To prevent temporal leakage, predictors were grouped by availability, and training-only feature selection identified three baseline and two first-year variables. NORIA jointly predicts baseline and updated glycemic control, an HbA1c change index, and 21 medication labels using shared representations, masked training, and stage-specific prediction updates. Comparators included classical machine learning, gradient boosting, deep tabular models, and multitask architectures (MMoE and PLE). On the internal test set, NORIA achieved AUROCs of 0.8554 and 0.8888 for baseline and updated glycemic control, respectively, and medication macro-AP of 0.1854 versus 0.1879 for CatBoost. The predefined medication improvement criterion was not met. With 20% of baseline features artificially masked, updated-control AUROC declined by 0.0271 for NORIA, versus 0.0510 for CatBoost and 0.0542 for FT-Transformer. Ablation analyses indicated that masked training provided the clearest robustness benefit. NORIA thus demonstrated competitive accuracy and robustness in selected simulated missing-data scenarios, without establishing overall superiority.

title: The Sign Code: The Hidden Binary Nature of Deep Networks
abstract: Every neuron in a trained network outputs a number that can be separated into its sign (positive or negative) and its magnitude (absolute size). We call the set of all neuron signs the \textit{sign code}. This raises a key question: does classification depend more on the sign code or on the magnitudes? For overparameterized vision classifiers with sign-preserving activations, the answer is overwhelmingly the sign code. A $k$-nearest neighbor classifier operating only on this binary sign code achieves accuracy comparable to the full model across different architectures, activation functions, and datasets. Moreover, replacing all magnitudes in every layer with random noise while keeping the original signs barely changes residual network performance. In contrast, flipping just 20\% of the signs reduces accuracy to chance. Models generalize well when same-class inputs share similar sign codes. When this overlap is disrupted by a regularizer, training accuracy remains high, but test performance collapses. A margin decomposition helps explain these results: the sign-only contribution to each logit grows as $\sqrt{d}$ in network width, dominating the magnitude residual. The natural unit of analysis for these networks may not be through their continuous weight space but instead through their discrete sign codes.

title: Suppression Is Not Erasure: A Dose Law for Representational Residue After Alignment Fine-Tuning
abstract: When a model that has learned a hidden behavior is fine-tuned to stop showing it, what exactly has been removed? We implant a trigger-flip backdoor into a small neural network, then apply graded doses of alignment fine-tuning and measure the residue simultaneously in three spaces: behavior, internal activations, and weights. The three decay at three different rates. At the largest dose (1600 steps), the behavior is essentially gone (trigger flip rate 0.0078, down from 0.964 implanted), yet 31% of the activation-level residue remains, and the weight-space scar is about 85% intact. The activation residue decays on a strictly monotone ladder and its decay decelerates, consistent with a nonzero floor. Alignment also does measurably more geometric surgery than dose-matched ordinary training. Four predictions were sealed before the run; two failed, and their failure magnitudes are reported as part of the result. The headline claims of the backdoor-persistence literature are behavioral; no quantitative dose law for representational residue was found in our sweep (October 16, 2026). This paper supplies one at toy scale, with its scope stated. © Adrian Alan Baillargeon — commercial use by permission.

title: Generative AI Decision Support in B2C E-Commerce: A Consumer Buying Behaviour Framework
abstract: Decision making in business-to-consumer (B2C) e-commerce connects company and consumer activities before, during and after purchase, whereas many existing generative artificial intelligence (GAI) applications focus on specific tasks or functions. This article develops a conceptual framework linking employee responsibilities, consumer choices, GAI support, information sources, permissions and two-sided evaluation through the five-stage Consumer Buying Behaviour (CBB) process. It connects need clarification, information gathering, feasible-offer comparison, transaction review and post-purchase assessment through decision gates and bounded support functions. Five employees and three consumers participated in a fixed-order ChatGPT 5.6 demonstration to examine the administration and perceived value of the proposed decision-support approach. Following a brief GAI introduction, participants observed ordinary prompt-response support and then a structured CBB-guided sequence within the same general e-commerce decision context. Questionnaire ratings were generally more favourable following CBB guidance, particularly for perceived comparison support and mental effort. The study-specific items are descriptive indicators, and fixed ordering confounds condition with practice, familiarity, novelty, fatigue, expectancy and task-set effects. The contribution is strictly conceptual and methodological; the eight-participant exercise supplies procedural illustration and design input, without establishing effectiveness, deployment readiness or validated system behaviour. Future evaluation requires an implemented system, versioned tasks and outputs, independently scored task-level records, and randomised or counterbalanced comparison.

title: Beyond Action Prediction: Learning Search-Free Planning in Latent Space
abstract: Latent world models learn action-conditioned state transitions in a compact representation space, providing a predictive model for visual planning and control. However, planning with these models typically requires costly test-time optimization over action sequences. We propose to replace this online search with a goal-conditioned inverse model that directly predicts actions from current and goal observations. A key challenge is that action prediction alone neither ensures that goal representations encode action-relevant information nor that predicted actions are consistent with the learned latent prediction model. We introduce Hindsight Inverse JEPA Planning (HIJP), a search-free framework that addresses both aspects during training. HIJP relabels future observations along offline trajectories as goals, providing action supervision across multiple temporal horizons. By retaining gradients through the goal representations, this supervision directly shapes the visual representation. HIJP further feeds predicted actions into the latent predictor model and aligns the resulting next-state representations with encoded successor observations, enforcing action-transition consistency. At inference time, the inverse dynamics model and latent predictor models are applied alternately to generate multi-step action sequences without online search. Across four visual control tasks, HIJP achieves 86.8% overall success and a 1.9-16.5x planning speedup over search-based planning.

title: Learning from the Learner's Response: Bi-Objective Acquisition for Sparse Expert Supervision in Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Sparse expert supervision can improve reinforcement learning, but deciding whichstates are worth annotating remains difficult. Uncertainty identifies where a learneris unsure, but does not directly identify where supervision will most stronglychange that learner. We introduce ALBERTA, a response-aware acquisition frame-work that measures local policy and value changes produced by controlled expertinterventions, predicts those responses from pre-annotation signals, and selectscandidates in the resulting two-dimensional response space. A calibration set of200 expert-labeled probes is used to learn response from policy entropy, historicalcritic disagreement, and their interaction; Pareto selection then allocates a separate121-state downstream budget. The response-aware branch therefore uses 321 ex-pert labels in total, compared with 121 for the Random baseline. In a controlledsingle-seed Atomic Chess experiment from a common RL10 branch point, thePareto branch achieves a higher mean game score than PPO-only at all four testedevaluation temperatures, with smaller margins at higher temperatures, and showsits largest margins over Random at lower temperatures. These results provideevidence that learner response can be a useful acquisition target while exposingsubstantial differences between policy and value responsiveness.

title: spectrace: real-engine validation of offline speculative-decoding pass-count prediction, and drafter selection for RL rollouts
abstract: Correction to v0.1.0/v0.1.1: the HF speculative-sampling comparison (27.36 predicted vs 27.28 measured) was off by one. It compared the estimator from position 1 with target calls minus one, but in HF assisted decoding the first target forward already verifies the first draft block. The rerun (real_sampling2) compares E[0] with the full call count, masks <|endoftext|> on both sides as min_new_tokens does, and doubles the runs: 28.28 predicted vs 28.23 measured passes (240 runs), +0.19%, paired 95% CI -1.45% to +1.84%. README and REPORT now describe this and the drafter-selection results as agreement within Monte Carlo noise, not sub-percent accuracy. Thanks to the authors of arXiv:2610.10411 for the review.

title: Gerenuk Optimization Algorithm: A Novel Nature-inspired Metaheuristic for Solving Optimization Problems
abstract: Complex optimization problems in many engineering and scientific applications require optimization methods that can achieve an effective balance between broad search and precise local search.In this study, the Gerenuk Optimization Algorithm (GOA) is introduced as a new metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of the Gerenuk.The main idea of GOA is based on two complementary behaviors of this animal: exploring different areas to identify suitable food sources and intensively exploiting promising food sources.These behaviors are modeled through two phases: exploration and exploitation.The exploration phase enhances global search by moving towards better food sources while simultaneously exploring new regions of the search space, whereas the exploitation phase performs local search and refinement around promising solutions.To evaluate the performance of GOA, 23 benchmark functions, including unimodal test functions (F1-F7), high-dimensional multimodal test functions (F8-F13), and fixed-dimensional multimodal test functions (F14-F23), are considered.GOA and nine competing algorithms are evaluated over 20 independent runs with 1000 iterations, and the mean, standard deviation (std), and rank are used as evaluation criteria.The results show that GOA ranked first among the compared optimizers on 19 out of 23 benchmark functions, corresponding to 82.61% of the test functions.The convergence curves and boxplots further demonstrate the solution quality, convergence behavior, and acceptable stability of GOA across a large proportion of the benchmark functions.Overall, the findings indicate that GOA, with its effective exploration and exploitation mechanisms and appropriate search balance, can serve as an effective optimization tool for a wide range of optimization problems and real-world applications.

title: Focus Pocus: Redirecting Technologically Distracted Students via Artificially Intelligent Characters
abstract: Digital learning environments challenge student attention, as notifications and low engagement cause students to drift from tasks, often without awareness. We present a system using real-time gaze tracking and screenshot analysis to detect distraction during digital exams and deliver timely, non-disruptive interventions via an on-screen character ("screenmate"). The system generates a continuous focus score by correlating where students look with what is displayed on their screen, and uses this score to trigger nudges when attention lapses are detected. We evaluated the system in a user study with 77 undergraduate students completing a 30-minute exam; results suggest that the gaze-derived focus score broadly tracks with students' subjective attention levels, though consistency varies across participants. Intervention analysis revealed a tension between effectiveness and intrusiveness — strong nudges successfully redirected focus but felt disruptive, while subtler cues preserved flow but were easier to ignore — pointing toward future work on richer behavioral signals and more adaptive, user-controlled interventions.

title: Trajectory-Triggered Sparse Collaborative Decoding
abstract: Dense assistance methods such as speculative decoding repeatedly verify draft tokens with a target model, keeping target computation coupled to generation. We study sparse collaborative decoding, where a draft model generates most tokens and a target model is invoked only for short corrective segments. The key problem is deciding when to call the target. We show that local uncertainty is a weak trigger: entropy, negative log-likelihood, logit margin, top-$k$ mass, and velocity features give near-chance failure prediction, with AUC 0.50-0.53. In contrast, aggregate trajectory-shape features over the draft confidence path reach AUC 0.86 using a lightweight logistic predictor trained only from draft correctness labels. This induces a trigger-timing tradeoff: early calls have more leverage but weaker evidence, while later calls have stronger evidence but less ability to redirect the trajectory. Used online, learned sparse collaborative decoding improves over the best open-loop schedule by +5.3 to +20.0 accuracy points across five GSM8K draft-target pairs. On MATH-500, it gains 7.0-13.5 points when early prediction and target competence align, but loses when either is weak. On StrategyQA, it improves over open-loop by 5.0-8.3 points, showing transfer beyond arithmetics.

title: A Predictive Operating-System Control Layer for Quantum Computing Hardware and Execution Stacks
abstract: Quantum processors exhibit time-varying hardwaredrift, environmental fluctuations, and correlated control errorsthat challenge reliable execution and increase the physical errorburden presented to higher-level error-correction procedures.Existing approaches address important aspects of quantumcalibration, feedback control, scheduling, and error correction,but these functions are typically studied and implemented asdistinct components. We introduce QID-OS (Quantum Intelligent Dynamic Operating System), an operating-system-levelcontrol-plane architecture for quantum execution that mediatesbetween physical hardware telemetry and higher-level compilation, runtime, and quantum error-correction services. QID-OSintegrates causal recursive least-squares (RLS) online parameterestimation, predictive pulse-level compensation, and adaptiveexecution scheduling within a closed-loop runtime architecture.The proposed framework is evaluated using a distance-3 surfacecode simulation under a specified non-Markovian noise model, afull-factorial 23 module ablation, and experiments on a 5-qubitconnected subset of an IBM Quantum superconducting processor.In simulation, QID-OS improves logical success probability overthe evaluated noise conditions, and the full configuration achievesthe highest success probability among the evaluated modulecombinations. On superconducting hardware, the experimentallyvalidated online RLS estimation and active pulse-compensationcomponents increase computational-basis success probabilityfrom 68.5% ± 0.4% to 88.4% ± 0.3% across three independent8-hour calibration windows, comprising 300 randomized testcircuits and 2,457,600 total measurement shots. These resultsdemonstrate the feasibility of using a predictive control-planearchitecture to mitigate hardware-level errors prior to higherlevel quantum error-correction processing.

abstract: First public release of the Dinfty Lean 4 formalization (toolchain leanprover/lean4:v4.32.2). title: Dataset and experimental materials for evaluating LLM reliability in transport planning
abstract: This dataset contains the experimental materials for a study on whether publicly accessible conversational large language models (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and Microsoft Copilot) can generate road freight driver schedules that comply with EU driving-time and rest-period rules (Regulation (EC) No 561/2006 and Regulation (EU) No 165/2014). A single international freight transport scenario was tested at four levels of prompt structuring, from an open-ended instruction to a highly controlled prompt with explicit rules, fixed assumptions and a prescribed output format. The dataset includes: the shared transport scenario used in all experimental conditions; the exact system-level and user-level prompts for each of the four prompt levels; execution metadata for each test, including platform, model version and run details; the complete, unedited responses generated by the evaluated models (64 responses in total). The tests were run between February and June 2026 in private or history-disabled chat modes. The materials are provided to support transparency, independent verification and replication of the reported findings.

title: What Determines the Direction of Post-Training Gains? A Preregistered Multi-Scale Study of Method, Scale, and Base-Model Identity
abstract: Preprint of the findings paper. Companion methods paper: "Benchmarking Post-Training Under Constrained Compute: Protocols for Question Generation, Variance-Controlled Evaluation, and Judge Auditing" (Zenodo, DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23409480). In an earlier pilot on a smaller single-judge pool, fine-tuning our own 4B model sharply lowered its perplexity on the target corpus without a corresponding gain in its judged score, motivating the question of what determines the direction and magnitude of the post-training gain. We answer it with a two-sided design: a within-family elasticity surface over four scale points crossed with three training methods, and two generalization probes, a second base family and a second task domain. The surface reverses the ordering of the two reinforcement-style methods between 4B and 9B (RLVR-C v2 ahead at 4B, MGPO-EG ahead at 9B) and yields one preregistered adjacent-granularity promotion, reported as a near-threshold result rather than a significance claim. Both probes return a gain-sign flip that tracks base-model identity, and an ablation demonstrates that the active ingredient of our momentum-perturbed optimizer is the perturbation itself.

title: An Alignment-Driven Approach for Constructing SPARQL Federated Queries
abstract: Integrating complementary information across distributed SPARQL endpoints remains a significant challenge. While query federation enables access across multiple endpoints, constructing federated queries requires both SPARQL expertise and knowledge of the underlying ontological schemas. Current query rewriting techniques primarily focus on vocabulary translation to retrieve equivalent data, often overlooking the integration of complementary information spread across sources. To address these limitations, we propose an alignment-driven approach that assists users in constructing federated queries by leveraging ontology alignments. Our approach joins class paths – user-selected sequences of ontology classes and relationships – from source and target ontologies, guided by alignment-based filtering, into a unified path that serves as the foundation for generating federated SPARQL queries capturing complementary aspects of the user’s intent. An experimental evaluation using OAEI Conference track datasets demonstrates that the generated queries consistently match reference queries in both structure and data retrieval across simple and complex mapping types, confirming the approach’s effectiveness in integrating complementary data from heterogeneous sources.

title: Particle swarm optimization-based type-2 fuzzy modeling for ECG signal prediction
abstract: A hybrid prediction framework based on Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and the Interval Type-2 Fuzzy Inference System (IT2FIS) is proposed in this paper. The major contribution is a systematic methodology for calculating the ideal parameter vector to tune the membership functions of a type-2 fuzzy controller. In contrast to type-1 fuzzy controllers, the interval type-2 formulation provides better robustness in uncertain operating conditions by explicitly modelling uncertainty through a Footprint of Uncertainty (FOU) bounded by upper and lower membership functions. Four performance indices mean square error (MSE), root mean square error (RMSE), error mean, and error standard deviation were used to assess the suggested IT2FIS-PSO framework on typical ECG arrhythmia signal data. The baseline IT2FIS produced an RMSE of 0.1198. This improved to 0.0429, a reduction of almost 75.98%, after PSO-based optimization of both membership function bounds. Experimental data show that the proposed optimization technique significantly improves ECG prediction accuracy relative to the unoptimized baseline, and simulation results confirm that PSO consistently finds the optimal parameters for a type-2 fuzzy controller.

title: SIT-Eval: Situation-Based Interactive Turn-by-Turn Evaluation of Conversational Agents
abstract: The rapid proliferation of conversational AI agents necessitates evaluation methods that assess performance across diverse dialogue scenarios, utilizing multiple situational criteria, as appropriate behavior depends on context and encompasses various aspects. Existing dialogue benchmarks typically use static natural conversations, which underrepresent rare situations---a critical safety gap, as low-probability events become frequent failures at production scale. However, limited sample sizes force a choice: either maintain natural dialogues for realism or turn to adaptive situation sampling for comprehensive yet statistically reliable coverage. We introduce SIT-Eval, an adjustable framework for evaluating situation-based conversational agents. We formalize an agent's desired behavior as situational rules: if situation is P, follow rules Q. At each conversation turn, an LLM-interlocutor enacts a uniformly sampled situation. A context-aware LLM-judge leverages all conditionally applicable rules as criteria to evaluate the agent's reply for that situation. The judge is validated using human-verified synthetic golden dialogues. Benchmarking 8 LLMs on 1292 conversation turns reveals failure modes hidden by aggregate metrics: models with similar overall scores vary widely in their adherence to individual rules. All models struggle most with ambiguity clarification and Socratic questioning.

title: Cross-lingual voice clone set, split lists, code and per-seed results for "Where Does Spoofing Evidence Live?"
abstract: Supplementary data and code for a study of where spoofing evidence resides in self-supervised speech representations, in German, English and French. Contains: (1) a cross-lingual voice clone set of 1,080 utterances (990 analysed) generated with XTTS v2, in which the language of the text and the native language of the cloned voice are fully crossed across six reference voices and sixty sentences per language; (2) the train/development/test file lists for MLAAD v12 and M-AILABS used in the paper, implementing a matched design with equal training utterances and speakers per language and one generator held out; (3) all generation, preprocessing, probing, training and analysis code; (4) per-seed results for every trained configuration, behind every statistical test in the paper. A verify_statistics.py script recomputes all 78 published values from the deposited results in a few seconds, without retraining. Audio is released under CC BY-NC 4.0, inherited from the XTTS v2 model licence; code under MIT. MLAAD and M-AILABS audio is not included — only file identifiers.

title: PV Impact Calculation (Haze) Guideline
abstract: This guideline provides a screening-level methodology for estimating photovoltaic (PV) energy and revenue losses caused by haze episodes in Malaysia. The methodology converts Air Pollutant Index (API) or PM2.5 concentrations into Aerosol Optical Depth (AOD), irradiance reduction, PV energy loss, and financial impact. The guideline is intended for risk management, sustainability, finance, asset management, audit, and energy professionals. It includes worked examples, uncertainty analysis, assumptions registers, and recommendations for Level 1, Level 2, and Level 3 assessments. Status: Proposed method. Not an official publication of the Department of Environment Malaysia (DOE), ISO, IEC, or Malaysian Standards.

title: Long-Term Memory for AI Characters: Memory, Context and Contextual Emotional Inference in AI Roleplay
abstract: An essay on long-term memory for AI characters, written by the founder of ChatBrat AI. It argues that useful AI character memory goes beyond storing facts: it combines conversational context, history and contextual emotional inference (tentative, revisable readings of conversational signals) so that remembered history changes how a character behaves. It distinguishes fact memory from experience memory, outlines what long-term memory should and should not keep, describes an observe-interpret-retrieve-compare-respond-update loop, and proposes practical tests for meaningful memory. It is an opinion and design essay, not an empirical study, and makes no product-performance claims.
